def profile_analysis( profile_file, trace_file=None, magnification=1.0, pixelsize=5.0, power=20.0, reprate=4.0, ROI_diam: int = 100, forced_background=None, trace_cutoff_radius=50.0, cutoff_gaus_fit_profile=25.0): 
135def profile_analysis(profile_file, trace_file = None, magnification=1., pixelsize=5., power=20., reprate=4., ROI_diam:int=100, forced_background=None, trace_cutoff_radius = 50., cutoff_gaus_fit_profile = 25.):
136    """if trace_file is None, this function only loads, fits and plots the beam profile; if trace_file is given, the function additionally calculates the peak intensity and field.
137
138    Args:
139        profile_file: name of the file containing the beam profile; the file (txt or csv) contains the 2D array of the beam profile
140        trace_file: None; name of the file containing the trace; the file (txt or csv) contains the time and field arrays as tab-separated columns
141        magnification: 1.; ratio of lens-camera/lens-z0 lengths; This is used to give the correct size of the beam profile at z0 in um
142        pixelsize: 5. um; pixel size of the camera
143        power: 20. mW; power of the laser beam; this is used to calculate the peak intensity
144        reprate: 4 kHz; repetition rate of the laser; this is used to calculate the peak intensity
145        ROI_diam: 100; diameter of the region of interest in pixels; the center of the ROI is the maximum of the camera data (which is assumed to be not saturated)
146        cutoff_gaus_fit_profile: 25. pixels; the 2d gaussian is fitted to the beam profile up to this distance from the peak
147        forced_background: None; if not None, the subtracted background is set to this value; otherwise it's computed from the outer ring of the ROI (camera data)
148        trace_cutoff_radius: 50. fs; for intensity calculation, the integral of the trace is computed only in the range t[peak]-trace_cutoff_radius < t < t[peak]+trace_cutoff_radius"""
149
150    pixelsize=pixelsize/magnification
151    data=pandas.read_csv(profile_file)
152
153    dataval=np.array(data.values)
154    #print('eliminating fixed broken pixels rayCi camera')
155    #dataval=eliminate_broken_pixels(dataval)
156    maxindex = np.unravel_index(np.argmax(dataval), dataval.shape)
157    print('diameter of Region Of Interest (ROI): ', ROI_diam, ' pixels')
158    dataval=np.array(data.values[maxindex[0]-int(ROI_diam/2):maxindex[0]+int(ROI_diam/2),maxindex[1]-int(ROI_diam/2):maxindex[1]+int(ROI_diam/2)])
159    maxindex = np.unravel_index(np.argmax(dataval), dataval.shape)
160
161    background = 0.
162    count = 0
163    print('calculating background intensity outside a circle whose diameter is 3/4 of the ROI diameter')
164    for i, j in np.ndindex(dataval.shape):
165        if (i-maxindex[0])**2 + (j-maxindex[1])**2 > (ROI_diam*3/8)**2:
166            background += dataval[i,j]
167            count += 1
168    background /= count
169
170    if forced_background is not None:
171        background = forced_background
172        print('subtracting background intensity: ', background)
173    else:
174        print('subtracting background intensity: ', background)
175
176    dataval=np.maximum(dataval-background, dataval*0.)
177    maxval = np.max(dataval)
178
179    # gaussian fit
180    param = moments_peak(dataval)
181    param = fitgaussian(cut_tail(dataval, cutoff_gaus_fit_profile))
182    X, Y = np.indices(dataval.shape)
183    fitted_funct = gaussian(*param)(X, Y)
184    print('beam w (um), resp. in x and y axis:', 2*param[3]*pixelsize, 2*param[4]*pixelsize)
185    print('beam 1/e^2 diameter [um]: ', 4*param[3]*pixelsize, 4*param[4]*pixelsize)
186
187    if  trace_file is not None:
188
189        trace = pandas.read_csv(trace_file, sep='\t')
190
191        # time in fs, field in a.u.
192        intensity = power *1e-3/reprate *1e-3\
193                / integral2d(fitted_funct, pixelsize=pixelsize) * np.max(fitted_funct) *1e8 \
194                / trace_integral(trace['delay (fs)'], cut_trace(trace['delay (fs)'], trace['field (a.u.)']**2, trace_cutoff_radius)) * np.max(trace['field (a.u.)']**2) *1e15
195
196        intensityFromRawCameraData = power *1e-3/reprate *1e-3\
197                / integral2d(dataval[maxindex[0]-int(ROI_diam/2):maxindex[0]+int(ROI_diam/2),maxindex[1]-int(ROI_diam/2):maxindex[1]+int(ROI_diam/2)], pixelsize=pixelsize) * np.max(dataval) *1e8 \
198                / trace_integral(trace['delay (fs)'], cut_trace(trace['delay (fs)'], trace['field (a.u.)']**2, trace_cutoff_radius)) * np.max(trace['field (a.u.)']**2) *1e15
199
200        temporal_fwhm = get_fwhm(np.array(trace['delay (fs)']), np.array(trace['field (a.u.)']))
201        intensityFromTemporalFWHM = power *1e-3/reprate *1e-3\
202                / integral2d(dataval[maxindex[0]-int(ROI_diam/2):maxindex[0]+int(ROI_diam/2),maxindex[1]-int(ROI_diam/2):maxindex[1]+int(ROI_diam/2)], pixelsize=pixelsize) * np.max(dataval) *1e8 \
203                / (np.sqrt(2*np.pi)*temporal_fwhm/np.sqrt(8*np.log(2))) *1e15
204
205        print('\nusing the gaussian fit of the beam profile and the integral of the trace^2:\n '
206            'peak intensity (sub-cycle, W/cm2): {i:.3e}'.format(**{'i':intensity}))
207        peak_field = np.sqrt(intensity*1e4 /constants.speed_of_light/constants.epsilon_0)
208        print('peak field (sub-cycle, V/m): {f:.3e}'.format(**{'f':peak_field}))
209
210        print('\nusing directly camera data, and the integral of the trace^2:\n '
211              'peak intensity (sub-cycle, W/cm2): {i:.3e}'.format(**{'i':intensityFromRawCameraData}))
212        peak_field = np.sqrt(intensityFromRawCameraData*1e4 /constants.speed_of_light/constants.epsilon_0)
213        print('peak field (sub-cycle, V/m): {f:.3e}'.format(**{'f':peak_field}))
214
215        print('\nusing directly camera data, and the temporal FWHM retrieved from the trace:\n '
216              'peak intensity (sub-cycle, W/cm2): {i:.3e}'.format(**{'i':intensityFromTemporalFWHM}))
217        peak_field = np.sqrt(intensityFromTemporalFWHM*1e4 /constants.speed_of_light/constants.epsilon_0)
218        print('peak field (sub-cycle, V/m): {f:.3e}'.format(**{'f':peak_field}))
219
220        fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 1)
221        time = trace['delay (fs)']
222        field = trace['field (a.u.)']
223        i_peak = np.argmax(field**2)
224        ax.plot(time[np.abs(time-time[i_peak])<trace_cutoff_radius],
225                field[np.abs(time-time[i_peak])<trace_cutoff_radius]**2)
226        plt.show()
227
228    fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 1)
229    ax.imshow(dataval)
230    plt.show()
231
232    plot_crosssect(dataval, fitfunct=gaussian(*param))

class TraceHandler: 
106class TraceHandler:
107    """Loads and stores the trace (field vs time) saved to file (two columns, tab separated) or given in the form of time and field [or wavelengths, spectrum and phase] arrays.
108
109    ALL THE TIMES ARE IN fs, FREQUENCIES IN PHz, WAVELENGTHS IN nm.
110
111    Most of the class methods modify the object data in place, and don't return anything.
112
113    Attributes:
114        fieldTimeV: (WAVEFORM DATA in the time domain) time array (fs)
115        fieldV: (WAVEFORM DATA in the time domain) field array
116        fieldStdevV: (WAVEFORM DATA in the time domain) field standard deviation (or sigma) array
117
118        frequencyAxis: (WAVEFORM DATA in the frequency domain) frequency axis of the FFT in PHz (should be np.fft compatible, i.e., equally spaced, in the form [0, df, 2*df, ..., fmax, -fmax[-df], ..., -df])
119        fftFieldV: (WAVEFORM DATA in the frequency domain) FFT field (complex)
120        complexFieldTimeV: (WAVEFORM DATA in the frequency domain) time axis of the complex field (fs)
121        complexFieldV: (WAVEFORM DATA in the frequency domain) complex field ( = IFFT{FFT(ω)θ(ω)}(t), where θ(ω) = 1 if ω >= 0, θ(ω) = 0 otherwise )
122        wvlAxis: (WAVEFORM DATA in the frequency domain) wavelength axis for the FFT spectrum (nm)
123        fftSpectrum: (WAVEFORM DATA in the frequency domain) wavelength-dependent positive FFT spectrum ( = |FFT{field}|^2 * df/dλ, λ > 0 )
124        fftphase: (WAVEFORM DATA in the frequency domain) wavelength-dependent spectral phase
125
126        wvlSpectrometer: (SPECTROMETER DATA) wavelength (nm)
127        ISpectrometer: (SPECTROMETER DATA) spectral intensity
128
129        fsZeroPadding: (= 150 by default) time span in fs for zero padding (appending zeroes both before and after the trace, in order to get a smoother fft)
130        filename: filename to load the trace from
131        filename_spectrum: filename to load the spectrum from
132        normalization_trace: normalization factor for the trace
133        zero_delay: time zero, corresponds to the maximum envelope
134    """
135    def __init__(self, filename=None, filename_spectrum=None, time=None, field=None, stdev=None, wvl=None, spectrum=None, wvl_FFT_trace=None, spectrum_FFT_trace=None, phase_FFT_trace=None):
136        """Constructor; loads the trace from file (or from time-field or wavelegth-spectrum-phase arrays) and stores it in the class.
137
138        One of the following must be provided (as a default all args are None):
139        * filename: the name of the file containing the trace (two columns, tab separated)
140        * time and field: the time vector (fs) and electric field vector (a.u.)
141        * wvl_FFT_trace, spectrum_FFT_trace and phase_FFT_trace: the wavelength (nm) spectrum (a.u.) and phase (rad) vectors
142
143        Args:
144            filename (str): the name of the file containing the trace (two columns - time and field, tab separated)
145            filename_spectrum (str): the name of the file containing the spectrum (two columns - wavelength and spectral intensity, tab separated)
146                this does not correspond to the fourier transform of the trace, but to some spectrometer data that you would like to compare to the loaded trace
147            time (array): the time vector (fs)
148            field (array): the electric field vector (a.u.)
149            stdev (array): the standard deviation (or sigma) of the electric field vector (a.u.)
150            wvl (array): the wavelength vector (nm) (spectrometer)
151            spectrum (array): the spectral intensity vector (a.u.) (spectrometer)
152            wvl_FFT_trace (array): the wavelength vector (nm) of the FFT trace (to reconstruct a trace from spectral data)
153            spectrum_FFT_trace (array): the spectral intensity vector (a.u.) of the FFT trace (to reconstruct a trace from spectral data)
154            phase_FFT_trace (array): the spectral phase vector (rad) of the FFT trace (to reconstruct a trace from spectral data)
155            """
156
157        self.fsZeroPadding = 150
158        self.filename = filename
159        self.filename_spectrum = filename_spectrum
160
161        self.fieldTimeV = None
162        self.fieldV = None
163        self.fieldStdevV = None
164
165        self.frequencyAxis = None
166        self.fftFieldV = None
167        self.complexFieldTimeV = None
168        self.complexFieldV = None
169        self.wvlAxis = None
170        self.fftSpectrum = None
171        self.fftphase = None
172
173        self.wvlSpectrometer = None
174        self.ISpectrometer = None
175
176        self.normalization_trace = None
177        self.zero_delay = None
178
179        if filename is not None:
180            self.load_trace()
181        elif time is not None and field is not None:
182            self.load_trace_from_arrays(time, field, stdev)
183        elif wvl_FFT_trace is not None and spectrum_FFT_trace is not None and phase_FFT_trace is not None:
184            self.load_trace_from_spectral_data(wvl_FFT_trace, spectrum_FFT_trace, phase_FFT_trace)
185        else:
186            print("\n\nWARNING: in function TraceHandler.__init__() no data was loaded\n\n")
187
188        if self.filename_spectrum is not None:
189            self.load_spectrum()
190        elif wvl is not None and spectrum is not None:
191            self.load_spectrum_from_arrays(wvl, spectrum)
192
193    def load_spectrum_from_arrays(self, wvl, spectrum):
194        """loads the spectrum from wavelength and spectrum arrays and stores it in the class.
195
196        The spectrum does not correspond to the fourier transform of the trace, but to some spectrometer data that you would like to compare with the loaded trace
197
198        Args:
199            wvl: wavelength array (nm)
200            spectrum: spectral intensity array
201        """
202        """wavelength is in nm"""
203        check_equal_length(wvl, spectrum)
204        self.wvlSpectrometer = np.array(wvl)
205        self.ISpectrometer = np.array(spectrum)
206
207    def load_trace_from_arrays(self, fieldTimeV, fieldV, fieldStdevV=None):
208        """loads the trace from time and field arrays and stores it in the class.
209
210        Args:
211            fieldTimeV: time array (fs)
212            fieldV: field array
213            fieldStdevV: standard deviation - or sigma - to be associated to the trace (optional, default = None)
214        """
215        if fieldTimeV is None or fieldV is None:
216            raise ValueError('\nin function TraceHandler.load_from_arrays() too many arguments were None\n'
217                             'it might be that the constructor was erroneously used with no or too few arguments\n')
218        if np.max(np.abs(fieldTimeV)) < 1.:
219            print('\n\nWARNING: do you remember that the time axis of TraceHandler is in fs?\n\n')
220        self.fieldTimeV = np.array(fieldTimeV)
221        self.fieldV = np.array(fieldV)
222        if fieldStdevV is not None:
223            self.fieldStdevV = np.array(fieldStdevV)
224        self.normalization_trace = np.max(np.abs(self.fieldV))
225        self.update_fft()
226
227    def load_trace(self, fname=None):
228        """loads from file"""
229        if fname is not None:
230            self.filename = fname
231        data = pandas.read_csv(self.filename, sep='\t')
232        self.fieldTimeV = data['delay (fs)'].to_numpy()
233        self.fieldV = data['field (a.u.)'].to_numpy()
234        self.fieldStdevV = data['stdev field'].to_numpy()
235        self.normalization_trace = np.max(np.abs(self.fieldV))
236        self.update_fft()
237
238    def load_trace_from_spectral_data(self, wvl_FFT_trace, spectrum_FFT_trace, phase_FFT_trace):
239        """loads the trace from wavelength, spectrum, and spectral phase arrays and stores it in the class.
240
241        This function has a different job than load_spectrum_from_arrays(): in fact, it retrieves the trace from the given spectral data via fourier transform.
242
243        Args:
244            wvl_FFT_trace: wavelength array in nm
245            spectrum_FFT_trace: (wavelength-)spectral intensity array. This is assumed to be |FFT{field}|^2 * df/dλ
246            phase_FFT_trace: spectral phase in rad
247        """
248        check_equal_length(wvl_FFT_trace, spectrum_FFT_trace, phase_FFT_trace)
249
250        # check that the wvl_FFT_trace array is monotonically increasing
251        if np.any(np.diff(wvl_FFT_trace) < 0):
252            if np.all(np.diff(wvl_FFT_trace) < 0):
253                wvl_FFT_trace = wvl_FFT_trace[::-1]
254                spectrum_FFT_trace = spectrum_FFT_trace[::-1]
255                phase_FFT_trace = phase_FFT_trace[::-1]
256            else:
257                raise ValueError('in function TraceHandler.load_from_spectral_data() wavelength array is not monotonous')
258
259        # frequency spectrum (monotonically increasing)
260        freq = constants.speed_of_light / wvl_FFT_trace[::-1] * 1e-6
261        spectrum_freq = spectrum_FFT_trace[::-1] / (constants.speed_of_light/wvl_FFT_trace[::-1]**2 *1e-6)
262        phase_FFT_trace = phase_FFT_trace[::-1]
263
264        # create proper freq axis for the fourier transform
265        df = (freq[1]-freq[0])/4
266        nf = int(np.ceil(3 * freq[-1]/df))
267        self.frequencyAxis = np.concatenate((np.arange(0, nf), np.arange(-nf, 0))) * df
268        # corresponding time window
269        twin = 1./(df)
270
271        # complex fourier transform
272        spectrum_freq = np.sqrt(spectrum_freq)*np.exp(1.j*phase_FFT_trace)
273
274        # fill with zeros
275        initial_zero_freq = np.linspace(freq[1]-freq[0], freq[0], int(np.ceil(4 * freq[0]/(freq[1]-freq[0]))))
276        initial_zeros = np.zeros(len(initial_zero_freq))
277        final_zero_freq = np.linspace(2*freq[-1]-freq[-2], 4 * freq[-1], int(np.ceil(15 * freq[-1]/(freq[-1]-freq[-2]))))
278        final_zeros = np.zeros(len(final_zero_freq))
279        freq = np.concatenate((initial_zero_freq, freq, final_zero_freq))
280        spectrum_freq = np.concatenate((initial_zeros, spectrum_freq, final_zeros))
281        # add negative frequencies
282        freq = np.concatenate((-freq[::-1], freq))
283        spectrum_freq = np.concatenate((np.conjugate(spectrum_freq[::-1]), spectrum_freq))
284
285        # interpolate the spectrum to the frequency axis of the fft
286        self.fftFieldV = np.interp(self.frequencyAxis, freq, spectrum_freq)
287
288        # add linear phase to center the pulse in the time window; this has to be done after interpolation because the spectral phase will be fast oscillating
289        self.fftFieldV = self.fftFieldV*np.exp(1.j*2*np.pi*self.frequencyAxis*twin/2)
290
291        self.update_fft_spectrum()
292        self.update_trace_from_fft()
293
294    def load_spectrum(self, fname=None):
295        """loads spectrum from file.
296
297        The spectrum does not correspond to the fourier transform of the trace, but to the spectrometer data that you would like to compare with the loaded trace
298
299        Args:
300            fname: filename
301        """
302        if fname is not None:
303            self.filename_spectrum = fname
304        data = pandas.read_csv(self.filename_spectrum, sep='\t')
305        self.wvlSpectrometer = data['wavelength (nm)'].to_numpy()
306        self.ISpectrometer = data['intensity (a.u.)'].to_numpy()
307        self.normalize_spectrum()
308
309    def update_fft(self, zero_pad_field = True):
310        """updates the fft of the trace from the time domain data.
311
312        Args:
313            zero_pad_field: bool; if true (default) add zeros before and after the trace before computing fft (for a smoother spectrum)
314                The length of appended zeros is defined by self.fsZeroPadding.
315        """
316        zp_fieldTimeV, zp_fieldV = deepcopy(self.fieldTimeV), deepcopy(self.fieldV)
317        if zero_pad_field:
318            zp_fieldTimeV, zp_fieldV = zero_padding(self.fieldTimeV, self.fieldV, fsExtension=self.fsZeroPadding)
319        self.frequencyAxis, self.fftFieldV = fourier_transform(zp_fieldTimeV, zp_fieldV)
320        self.update_fft_spectrum()
321
322    def update_fft_spectrum(self):
323        """Updates the wavelength-dependent intensity spectrum. Results are stored in self.wvlAxis and self.fftSpectrum.
324
325        This is (derived from but) different from the fourier transform because:
326         * it considers the squared modulus of the field
327         * it multiplies the frequency-dependent spectral density by df/dλ = c/λ²
328         * it considers only positive wavelengths
329
330        The function internally calls update_spectral_phase() as well.
331        """
332        self.wvlAxis = constants.speed_of_light/self.frequencyAxis[self.frequencyAxis > 0]*1.e-6
333        self.fftSpectrum = np.abs(self.fftFieldV[self.frequencyAxis > 0])**2 * constants.speed_of_light/self.wvlAxis**2
334        self.compute_complex_field()
335        self.update_spectral_phase()
336        self.normalize_fft_spectrum()
337
338    def update_spectral_phase(self):
339        """computes the spectral phase of the trace. The result is stored in self.fftphase.
340
341        An attempt of automatic linear phase subtraction is made. Phase is unwrapped.
342        """
343        # determine the time distance (delay) of the waveform peak from the beginning of the trace (more precisely, from the beginning of the ifft)
344        tmax = self.get_zero_delay()
345        deltaT1 = tmax - self.complexFieldTimeV[0]
346        deltaT2 = self.complexFieldTimeV[-1] - tmax
347        ifft_twindow = 1/ (self.frequencyAxis[1] - self.frequencyAxis[0])
348        total_delay = ifft_twindow/2 + (deltaT2-deltaT1)/2 # total estimated delay of the peak from the beginning of the ifft trace
349
350        # compute the phase, use the computed 'delay' to correct for the non-interesting linear component, and unwrap it
351        self.fftphase = np.angle(self.fftFieldV[self.frequencyAxis > 0])
352        self.fftphase = self.fftphase - total_delay * self.frequencyAxis[self.frequencyAxis > 0] * 2 * np.pi
353        self.fftphase = np.unwrap(self.fftphase)
354
355        # subtract constant phase offset (m * 2*π)
356        n_pi =  np.sum(self.fftSpectrum*self.fftphase)/ np.sum(self.fftSpectrum)
357        n_pi = int( n_pi / ( 2*np.pi ))
358        self.fftphase -= n_pi * 2 * np.pi
359
360
361    def update_trace_from_fft(self):        # remember to use together with strip_from_trace
362                                            # careful: the complex part of the IFFT is discarded
363        """Updates the field trace from fft
364
365        In most cases, you might want to call strip_from_trace() afterward, to eliminate the zero-padding from the trace.
366        """
367        self.fieldTimeV, self.fieldV = inverse_fourier_transform(self.frequencyAxis, self.fftFieldV)
368        self.fieldV = np.real(self.fieldV)
369        self.normalization_trace = np.max(np.abs(self.fieldV))
370        self.get_zero_delay()
371
372    def strip_from_trace(self, timeRange = None):
373        """eliminates the zeros appended to the trace (zero-padding) when computing the FFT.
374
375        Useful when retrieving the trace via ifft (method update_trace_from_fft()).
376
377        Args:
378            timeRange (float): the time range (fs) to strip from the beginning and end of the trace. If None (default), fsZeroPadding is used.
379        """
380        if timeRange is None:
381            timeRange = self.fsZeroPadding
382        # strip the first and last fsZeroPadding time points
383        self.fieldV = self.fieldV[(self.fieldTimeV >= np.min(self.fieldTimeV) + timeRange)
384                                          & (self.fieldTimeV <= np.max(self.fieldTimeV) - timeRange)]
385        self.fieldTimeV = self.fieldTimeV[(self.fieldTimeV >= np.min(self.fieldTimeV) + timeRange)
386                                          & (self.fieldTimeV <= np.max(self.fieldTimeV) - timeRange)]
387        if self.fieldStdevV is None:
388            return True
389        if len(self.fieldStdevV) > len(self.fieldV):
390            n_remove = len(self.fieldStdevV)-len(self.fieldV)
391            print('\n\nWarning: fieldStdevV is longer than fieldV, removing', n_remove, ' elements\n\n')
392            while n_remove > 0:
393                if n_remove % 2 == 0:
394                    self.fieldStdevV = np.delete(self.fieldStdevV, 0)
395                else:
396                    self.fieldStdevV = np.delete(self.fieldStdevV, -1)
397                n_remove -= 1
398        elif len(self.fieldStdevV) < len(self.fieldV):
399            n_add = len(self.fieldV)-len(self.fieldStdevV)
400            print('\n\nWarning: fieldStdevV is shorter than fieldV, adding', n_add, ' elements\n\n')
401            while n_add > 0:
402                if n_add % 2 == 0:
403                    self.fieldStdevV = np.insert(self.fieldStdevV, 0, 0)
404                else:
405                    self.fieldStdevV = np.append(self.fieldStdevV, 0)
406                n_add -= 1
407        return True
408
409    def strip_from_complex_trace(self, timeRange = None):
410        """from the complex trace eliminates the zeros appended (zero-padding) when computing the FFT (Analogous to strip_from_trace())."""
411        if timeRange is None:
412            timeRange = self.fsZeroPadding
413        # strip the first and last fsZeroPadding time points
414        self.complexFieldV= self.complexFieldV[(self.complexFieldTimeV >= np.min(self.complexFieldTimeV) + timeRange)
415                                          & (self.complexFieldTimeV <= np.max(self.complexFieldTimeV) - timeRange)]
416        self.complexFieldTimeV = self.complexFieldTimeV[(self.complexFieldTimeV >= np.min(self.complexFieldTimeV) + timeRange)
417                                          & (self.complexFieldTimeV <= np.max(self.complexFieldTimeV) - timeRange)]
418
419    def tukey_time_window(self, lowEdge, upEdge, lowEdgeWidth, upEdgeWidth):
420        """applies a tukey window to the trace in the time domain.
421
422        Args:
423            lowEdge, upEdge: lower and upper edge of the window upEdge-lowEdge = FWHM of the window
424            lowEdgeWidth, upEdgeWidth: width of the cosine-shaped edges (from 0 to 1 or viceversa)
425        """
426        window = asymmetric_tukey_window(np.abs(self.fieldTimeV), lowEdge, upEdge, lowEdgeWidth, upEdgeWidth)
427        self.fieldV = self.fieldV * window
428        self.update_fft()
429
430    def fourier_interpolation(self, ntimes_finer: int):
431        """Shrinks the time step of the trace in time domain by a factor ntimes_finer.
432
433        This is done by 'zero-padding' the fourier transform of the trace, i.e., by extending the frequency axis by a factor ntimes_finer, and adding corresponding zeros to the FFT field.
434
435        Args:
436            ntimes_finer (int): the factor by which to shrink the time step of the trace in time domain. Must be >= 1.
437        """
438        if ntimes_finer < 1:
439            raise ValueError('in function TraceHandler.fourier_interpolation() ntimes_finer must be >= 1')
440        if self.frequencyAxis is None or self.fftFieldV is None:
441            raise ValueError('in function TraceHandler.fourier_interpolation() frequency axis or fft field is not defined')
442        # extend the frequency axis by a factor ntimes_finer
443        df = self.frequencyAxis[1] - self.frequencyAxis[0]
444        i_last_pos = int(np.ceil(len(self.frequencyAxis) / 2) - 1)
445        if self.frequencyAxis[i_last_pos] < 0 or self.frequencyAxis[i_last_pos + 1] > 0:
446            print(self.frequencyAxis[0:i_last_pos + 1])
447            print(self.frequencyAxis[i_last_pos + 1:])
448            raise Exception('in function fourier_interpolation() frequency axes was not extended correctly')
449
450        appended_freqFFT = np.linspace(self.frequencyAxis[i_last_pos] + df, ntimes_finer * self.frequencyAxis[i_last_pos] + df,
451                                       round((ntimes_finer - 1) * self.frequencyAxis[i_last_pos] / df))
452        prepended_freqFFT = np.linspace(-(ntimes_finer - 1) * self.frequencyAxis[i_last_pos] + self.frequencyAxis[i_last_pos + 1],
453                                        +self.frequencyAxis[i_last_pos + 1], round((ntimes_finer - 1) * self.frequencyAxis[i_last_pos] / df))
454        self.frequencyAxis = np.concatenate(
455            (self.frequencyAxis[:i_last_pos + 1], appended_freqFFT, prepended_freqFFT, self.frequencyAxis[i_last_pos + 1:]))
456        self.fftFieldV = np.concatenate(
457            (self.fftFieldV[:i_last_pos + 1], np.zeros(len(appended_freqFFT)), np.zeros(len(prepended_freqFFT)),
458             self.fftFieldV[i_last_pos + 1:]))
459
460        self.update_trace_from_fft()
461        self.strip_from_trace()
462        self.update_fft_spectrum()
463
464    def differentiate_trace(self, spectrally=True):
465        """computes the time derivative of the trace.
466
467        Args:
468            spectrally: bool; if True (default) the derivative will be computed in the spectral domain (maybe more stable numerically)
469        """
470        if spectrally:
471            self.fftFieldV = 1j * self.frequencyAxis * self.fftFieldV
472            self.update_trace_from_fft()
473            self.update_fft_spectrum()
474        else:
475            self.fieldV = np.gradient(self.fieldV, self.fieldTimeV)
476            self.update_fft()
477
478    def integrate_trace(self, spectrally=True):
479        """integrates the trace in time.
480
481        Args:
482            spectrally (bool): if True (default) the integral will be computed in the spectral domain (maybe more stable numerically)
483        """
484        if spectrally:
485            if self.frequencyAxis[0] != 0:
486                print('WARNING: in function TraceHandler.integrate_trace() the FFT axis\' first element is not zero')
487            self.fftFieldV[1:] = -1j / self.frequencyAxis[1:] * self.fftFieldV[1:]
488            self.update_trace_from_fft()
489            self.update_fft_spectrum()
490        else:
491            self.fieldV = np.cumsum(self.fieldV) * np.mean(np.diff(self.fieldTimeV))
492            self.update_fft()
493
494    def save_trace_to_file(self, filename, low_lim=None, up_lim=None):
495        """Saves the trace to file
496
497        Args:
498            filename
499            low_lim, up_lim: only save the trace between low_lim and up_lim (default: None, None)
500        """
501        if low_lim is not None and up_lim is not None:
502            fieldTimeV_to_write = self.fieldTimeV[(self.fieldTimeV >= low_lim) & (self.fieldTimeV <= up_lim)]
503            fieldV_to_write = self.fieldV[(self.fieldTimeV >= low_lim) & (self.fieldTimeV <= up_lim)]
504        else:
505            fieldTimeV_to_write = self.fieldTimeV
506            fieldV_to_write = self.fieldV
507        data = pandas.DataFrame({'delay (fs)': fieldTimeV_to_write, 'field (a.u.)': fieldV_to_write})
508        data.to_csv(filename, sep='\t', index=False)
509
510    def normalize_spectrum(self):
511        """Normalizes the comparison spectrum to its integral."""
512        spectrum_range = [60, 930]
513        n_factor = (np.abs(np.diff(self.wvlSpectrometer)[(self.wvlSpectrometer[:-1] > spectrum_range[0]) & (
514                    self.wvlSpectrometer[:-1] < spectrum_range[1])]) *
515                               self.ISpectrometer[:-1][(self.wvlSpectrometer[:-1] > spectrum_range[0]) & (
516                                       self.wvlSpectrometer[:-1] < spectrum_range[1])]).sum()
517        self.ISpectrometer /= n_factor
518
519    def normalize_fft_spectrum(self, spectrum_range = [60, 930]):
520        """Normalizes the spectrum of the trace (|FFT{trace}|^2 * df/dλ) to its integral (area)
521
522        Args:
523            spectrum_range (list): the range of wavelengths (nm) to consider for the normalization. Default is [60, 930] nm.
524        """
525        n_factor = (np.abs(np.diff(self.wvlAxis)[(self.wvlAxis[:-1] > spectrum_range[0]) & (
526                    self.wvlAxis[:-1] < spectrum_range[1])]) *
527                               self.fftSpectrum[:-1][(self.wvlAxis[:-1] > spectrum_range[0]) & (
528                                       self.wvlAxis[:-1] < spectrum_range[1])]).sum()
529        self.fftSpectrum /= n_factor
530
531    def get_trace(self):
532        """Returns the time (fs) and field arrays. Field is in a.u. unless set_fluence() was called or a calibrated field was given as an input."""
533        return self.fieldTimeV, self.fieldV
534
535    def get_spectrum_trace(self):
536        """Returns the wavelength and spectral intensity corresponding to the fourier transform of the trace."""
537        return self.wvlAxis, self.fftSpectrum
538
539    def get_spectral_phase(self):
540        """Returns the wavelength array and the spectral phase array corresponding to the FFT of the trace."""
541        return self.wvlAxis, self.fftphase
542
543    def get_stdev(self):
544        """Returns only the standard deviation (sigma) array"""
545        return self.fieldStdevV
546
547    def get_positive_fft_field(self):
548        """Returns the positive frequency axis f and the corresponding FFT field (complex).
549
550        Main task of this function is to 'smooth' the phase of the fft (= remove linear phase, corresponding to a time shift in the temporal domain), since the waveform is usually centered around t = 0"""
551        if self.frequencyAxis is None or self.fftFieldV is None:
552            raise ValueError('in function TraceHandler.get_positive_fft_field() frequency axis or fft field is not defined')
553        positive_freq = self.frequencyAxis[self.frequencyAxis >= 0]
554        positive_fft_field = self.fftFieldV[self.frequencyAxis >= 0]
555        # remove linear phase
556        tmax = self.get_zero_delay()
557        deltaT1 = tmax - self.fieldTimeV[0]
558        deltaT2 = self.fieldTimeV[-1] - tmax
559        ifft_twindow = 1 / (self.frequencyAxis[1] - self.frequencyAxis[0])
560        total_delay = ifft_twindow / 2 + (deltaT2 - deltaT1) / 2
561        positive_fft_field = positive_fft_field * np.exp(-1.j * 2 * np.pi * positive_freq * total_delay)
562        return positive_freq, positive_fft_field
563
564    def get_fluence(self):
565        """Calculates the fluence of the trace.
566
567        convention: field [V/Å], time [fs], fluence [J/cm²]
568        F = c eps_0 integral(E^2)dt
569
570
571        Returns:
572            fluence: float
573        """
574        F = constants.speed_of_light*constants.epsilon_0 * np.trapz(self.fieldV**2, self.fieldTimeV)* 1e1
575        return F
576
577    def set_fluence(self, fluence):
578        """Set the fluence of the trace.
579
580        Convention: field [V/Å], time [fs], fluence [J/cm²]
581
582        F = c eps_0 integral(E^2)dt"""
583        F = constants.speed_of_light*constants.epsilon_0 * np.trapz(self.fieldV**2, self.fieldTimeV)* 1e1
584        self.fieldV *= np.sqrt(fluence/F)
585        self.update_fft()
586        self.update_fft_spectrum()
587
588    def compute_complex_field(self):
589        """Computes the complex trace by inverting the positive-freq FFT and stores it in self.complexFieldV (for envelope or phase computation, for example)
590
591        Notice that the fourier transform of the trace is not computed, it is assumed to be already stored in the class. This should be true in most cases."""
592        complex_spectrum = deepcopy(self.fftFieldV)
593        complex_spectrum[self.frequencyAxis < 0] = 0
594        self.complexFieldTimeV, self.complexFieldV= inverse_fourier_transform(self.frequencyAxis, complex_spectrum)
595        self.complexFieldV = 2* self.complexFieldV
596        self.strip_from_complex_trace()
597
598    def get_envelope(self):
599        """Get the envelope of the trace.
600
601        Returns:
602            time array (fs)
603            envelope array
604            """
605        if self.complexFieldV is None:
606            self.compute_complex_field()
607        return self.complexFieldTimeV, np.abs(self.complexFieldV)
608
609    def get_phase(self):
610        """Get the instantaneous phase of the trace.
611
612        If complexFieldV is already computed and stored, no re-calculation occurs
613
614        Returns:
615            time array (fs)
616            instantaneous phase array (fs)
617        """
618        if self.complexFieldV is None:
619            self.compute_complex_field()
620        return self.complexFieldTimeV, np.angle(self.complexFieldV)
621
622    def get_zero_delay(self):
623        """Get the time value corresponding to the envelope peak.
624
625        Returns:
626
627            zero_delay: float
628        """
629        # careful: the time grid should be fine enough to resolve the maximum of the envelope
630        t, en = self.get_envelope()
631        dt = t[1]-t[0]
632        max_index, max_value = find_maximum_location(en)
633        self.zero_delay = t[0] + dt * max_index
634        return self.zero_delay
635
636    def get_FWHM(self):
637        """get the FWHM of the trace.
638
639
640        Returns:
641            FWHM: float
642        """
643        t, en = self.get_envelope()
644        dt = t[1] - t[0]
645        return fwhm(en**2, dt)
646
647    def fft_tukey_bandpass(self, lowWavelengthEdge, upWavelengthEdge, lowEdgeWidth, highEdgeWidth):
648        """Applies a bandpass filter to the trace in the frequency domain using a tukey window.
649
650        The tukey window is 1 between  lowWavelengthEdge+lowEdgeWidth/2  and  upWavelengthEdge-highEdgeWidth/2
651        and it is reaches zero at lowWavelengthEdge-lowEdgeWidth/2  and  upWavelengthEdge+highEdgeWidth/2.
652        Notice that the edges are only cosine-shaped in the frequency domain. In the wavelength domain upWavelengthEdge - lowWavelengthEdge does not coincide with the FWHM of the tukey function
653
654        Args:
655            lowWavelengthEdge: float (nm)
656            upWavelengthEdge: float (nm)
657            lowEdgeWidth: float (nm)
658            highEdgeWidth: float (nm)
659        """
660        upFreqEdge = constants.speed_of_light / (lowWavelengthEdge - lowEdgeWidth / 2) /2 * 1e-6 + constants.speed_of_light / (
661                    lowWavelengthEdge + lowEdgeWidth / 2) /2 * 1e-6
662        lowFreqEdge = constants.speed_of_light / (upWavelengthEdge - highEdgeWidth / 2) /2 * 1e-6 + constants.speed_of_light / (
663                    upWavelengthEdge + highEdgeWidth / 2) /2 * 1e-6
664
665        upFreqEdgeWidth = constants.speed_of_light / (lowWavelengthEdge - lowEdgeWidth / 2) * 1e-6 - constants.speed_of_light / (
666                    lowWavelengthEdge + lowEdgeWidth / 2) * 1e-6
667        lowFreqEdgeWidth = constants.speed_of_light / (upWavelengthEdge - highEdgeWidth / 2) * 1e-6 - constants.speed_of_light / (
668                    upWavelengthEdge + highEdgeWidth / 2) * 1e-6
669
670        window = asymmetric_tukey_window(np.abs(self.frequencyAxis), lowFreqEdge, upFreqEdge, lowFreqEdgeWidth,
671                                         upFreqEdgeWidth)
672        self.fftFieldV = self.fftFieldV * window
673        self.update_trace_from_fft()
674        self.update_fft_spectrum()
675        self.strip_from_trace()
676
677    def apply_transmission(self, wavelengths, f):
678        """Applies a spectral transmission function to the trace (e.g. spectral filter).
679
680        Args:
681            wavelengths: ndarray = wavelength array (nm)
682            f: ndarray = transmission function f(λ)
683        """
684        if np.any(np.diff(wavelengths)) < 0:
685            if np.all(np.diff(wavelengths)) < 0:
686                wavelengths = wavelengths[::-1]
687                f = f[::-1]
688            else:
689                raise ValueError('in function TraceHandler.apply_transmission() wavelength array is not monotonous')
690        freq = constants.speed_of_light / wavelengths[::-1] * 1e-6
691        spectrum_freq = f[::-1]
692
693        # fill with zeros
694        initial_zero_freq = np.linspace(freq[1]-freq[0], freq[0], int(np.ceil(4 * freq[0]/(freq[1]-freq[0]))))
695        initial_zeros = np.zeros(len(initial_zero_freq))
696        final_zero_freq = np.linspace(2*freq[-1]-freq[-2], 4 * freq[-1], int(np.ceil(15 * freq[-1]/(freq[-1]-freq[-2]))))
697        final_zeros = np.zeros(len(final_zero_freq))
698        freq = np.concatenate((initial_zero_freq, freq, final_zero_freq))
699        spectrum_freq = np.concatenate((initial_zeros, spectrum_freq, final_zeros))
700        # add negative frequencies
701        freq = np.concatenate((-freq[::-1], freq))
702        spectrum_freq = np.concatenate((spectrum_freq[::-1], spectrum_freq))
703
704        #interpolate the spectrum to the frequency axis of the fft
705        spectrum_interp = np.interp(self.frequencyAxis, freq, spectrum_freq)
706
707        self.fftFieldV = self.fftFieldV * spectrum_interp
708        self.update_trace_from_fft()
709        self.update_fft_spectrum()
710        self.strip_from_trace()
711
712    def apply_spectrum(self, wvl = None , spectrum = None, CEP_shift: float = 0., stripZeroPadding: bool = True):
713        """Applies a spectrum to the phase of the trace. This means that a new trace is computed and stored in the TraceHandler object (replacing the existing one);
714        the new trace has spectral intensity equal to the applied spectrum and spectral phase equal to the phase of the existing trace.
715
716        Args:
717            wvl: wavelength array (nm). If None (default) the comparison spectrum stored in the class (self.wvlSpectrometer and self.ISpectrometer) is applied.
718            spectrum: spectral intensity array. If None (default) the comparison spectrum stored in the class (self.wvlSpectrometer and self.ISpectrometer) is applied.
719            CEP_shift: a possible artificial phase shift IN UNITS OF PI! (default = 0)
720            stripZeroPadding (bool): whether to eliminate the zero padding (zeros appended to the trace). Default is True"""
721
722        if wvl is None or spectrum is None:
723            wvl = self.wvlSpectrometer
724            spectrum = self.ISpectrometer
725        # check that the wvl array is monotonically increasing
726        if np.any(np.diff(wvl) < 0):
727            if np.all(np.diff(wvl) < 0):
728                wvl = wvl[::-1]
729                spectrum = spectrum[::-1]
730            else:
731                raise ValueError('in function TraceHandler.apply_spectrum() wavelength array is not monotonous')
732
733        # frequency spectrum (monotonically increasing)
734        freq = constants.speed_of_light / wvl[::-1] *1e-6
735        spectrum_freq = spectrum[::-1] / (constants.speed_of_light/wvl[::-1]**2 *1e-6)
736        spectrum_freq = np.maximum(spectrum_freq, np.zeros(len(spectrum_freq)))
737
738        # fill with zeros
739        initial_zero_freq = np.linspace(freq[1]-freq[0], freq[0], int(np.ceil(4 * freq[0]/(freq[1]-freq[0]))))
740        initial_zeros = np.zeros(len(initial_zero_freq))
741        final_zero_freq = np.linspace(2*freq[-1]-freq[-2], 4 * freq[-1], int(np.ceil(15 * freq[-1]/(freq[-1]-freq[-2]))))
742        final_zeros = np.zeros(len(final_zero_freq))
743        freq = np.concatenate((initial_zero_freq, freq, final_zero_freq))
744        spectrum_freq = np.concatenate((initial_zeros, spectrum_freq, final_zeros))
745        # add negative frequencies
746        freq = np.concatenate((-freq[::-1], freq))
747        spectrum_freq = np.concatenate((spectrum_freq[::-1], spectrum_freq))
748
749        # interpolate the spectrum to the frequency axis of the fft
750        spectrum_interp = np.interp(self.frequencyAxis, freq, spectrum_freq)
751        self.fftFieldV = np.sqrt(spectrum_interp)*np.exp(1j*np.angle(self.fftFieldV) + 1j*np.pi*CEP_shift*np.sign(self.frequencyAxis))
752
753
754        self.update_trace_from_fft()
755        if stripZeroPadding:
756            self.strip_from_trace()
757        else:
758            self.fieldStdevV = None
759        self.update_fft_spectrum()
760
761    def fresnel_reflection(self, material2, angle_in, material1=None, forward: bool=True, s_polarized: bool=True, path: str = "./RefractiveIndices/"):
762        """calculates the fresnel reflection of the pulse at the interface between two materials. The waveform is travelling from material 1 to material 2.
763        The first medium (material1) should be non-absorptive. As usual the resulting waveform is stored in the TraceHandler object, replacing the previous one.
764
765        Refractive index files should contain 3 space-separated columns, respectively with headers: wvl n k, where wvl is the wavelength in um, n and k resp. the real and imaginary part of the refractive index.
766        Args:
767            material2: the filename (without '.txt') of the refractive index data for the material after the interface (e.g. Si Al MgF2); wavelength is in um in the refractive index file
768            angle_in: the incidence angle in degrees
769            material1: the filename (without '.txt') of the refractive index data for the material before the interface. If None (default), vacuum is assumed
770            forward (bool):  if True (default) forward reflection is computed (the result waveform is the reflection of the previously stored waveform.
771
772                if False backward reflection is computed (the previous waveform is the reflection of the result waveform)
773            s_polarized (bool): True. Reflection calculation only implemented for s-polarized light
774            path (str): path for the refractive index files. Defaults to "./RefractiveIndices/"
775            """
776        if not s_polarized:
777            raise ValueError('in function TraceHandler.fresnel_reflection() p_polarized is not implemented yet\n')
778
779        # read refractive index
780        refIndexData = pandas.read_table(path + material2 + ".txt", sep=" ", keep_default_na=False)
781        wvl2 = np.array(refIndexData['wvl']) * 1e3
782        n2 = np.array(refIndexData['n']) +1j* np.array(refIndexData['k'])
783        if material1 is None:
784            wvl1 = np.array(wvl2)
785            n1 = n2*0 + 1
786        else:
787            refIndexData = pandas.read_table(path + material1 + ".txt", sep=" ", keep_default_na=False)
788            wvl1 = np.array(refIndexData['wvl']) * 1e3
789            n1 = np.array(refIndexData['n']) +1j* np.array(refIndexData['k'])
790
791        # check that the wvl arrays are monotonically increasing
792        if np.any(np.diff(wvl1) < 0):
793            if np.all(np.diff(wvl1) < 0):
794                wvl1 = wvl1[::-1]
795                n1 = n1[::-1]
796            else:
797                raise ValueError('in function TraceHandler.fresnel_reflection() wavelength array is not monotonous')
798        if np.any(np.diff(wvl2) < 0):
799            if np.all(np.diff(wvl2) < 0):
800                wvl2 = wvl2[::-1]
801                n2 = n2[::-1]
802            else:
803                raise ValueError('in function TraceHandler.fresnel_reflection() wavelength array is not monotonous')
804
805        # frequency spectrum (monotonically increasing)
806        freq1 = constants.speed_of_light / wvl1[::-1] * 1e-6
807        freq2 = constants.speed_of_light / wvl2[::-1] * 1e-6
808        n1 = n1[::-1]
809        n2 = n2[::-1]
810
811        # fill with ones
812        initial_ones_freq = np.linspace(freq1[1] - freq1[0], freq1[0], int(np.ceil(4 * freq1[0] / (freq1[1] - freq1[0]))))
813        initial_ones = np.ones(len(initial_ones_freq)) * n1[0]
814        final_ones_freq = np.linspace(2 * freq1[-1] - freq1[-2], 4 * freq1[-1],
815                                      int(np.ceil(15 * freq1[-1] / (freq1[-1] - freq1[-2]))))
816        final_ones = np.ones(len(final_ones_freq)) * n1[-1]
817        freq1 = np.concatenate((initial_ones_freq, freq1, final_ones_freq))
818        n1 = np.concatenate((initial_ones, n1, final_ones))
819        # same for n2
820        initial_ones_freq = np.linspace(freq2[1] - freq2[0], freq2[0], int(np.ceil(4 * freq2[0] / (freq2[1] - freq2[0]))))
821        initial_ones = np.ones(len(initial_ones_freq))* n2[0]
822        final_ones_freq = np.linspace(2 * freq2[-1] - freq2[-2], 4 * freq2[-1],
823                                        int(np.ceil(15 * freq2[-1] / (freq2[-1] - freq2[-2]))))
824        final_ones = np.ones(len(final_ones_freq)) * n2[-1]
825        freq2 = np.concatenate((initial_ones_freq, freq2, final_ones_freq))
826        n2 = np.concatenate((initial_ones, n2, final_ones))
827
828        # add negative frequencies
829        freq1 = np.concatenate((-freq1[::-1], freq1))
830        n1 = np.concatenate((np.conjugate(n1[::-1]), n1))
831        freq2 = np.concatenate((-freq2[::-1], freq2))
832        n2 = np.concatenate((np.conjugate(n2[::-1]), n2))
833
834        # interpolate the n1 and n2 to the frequency axis of the fft
835        n1Interp = np.interp(self.frequencyAxis, freq1, n1)
836        n2Interp = np.interp(self.frequencyAxis, freq2, n2)
837
838        # calculate the fresnel reflection coefficients using only the angle of incidence (NOT SURE THIS WORKS WHEN THE FIRST MEDIUM IS LOSSY)
839        r = ((n1Interp * np.cos(angle_in*np.pi/180) - n2Interp * np.sqrt(1-(n1Interp/n2Interp*np.sin(angle_in*np.pi/180))**2)) /
840             (n1Interp * np.cos(angle_in*np.pi/180) + n2Interp * np.sqrt(1-(n1Interp/n2Interp*np.sin(angle_in*np.pi/180))**2)))
841        if forward:
842            self.fftFieldV = self.fftFieldV * r
843        else:
844            self.fftFieldV = self.fftFieldV / r
845
846        self.fieldStdevV = None
847
848        self.update_trace_from_fft()
849        self.strip_from_trace()
850        self.update_fft_spectrum()
851
852
853    def apply_zero_phase(self):
854        """Applies zero-phase to the trace; this allows, for example, to retrieve the fourier limited pulse corresponding to the same FFT spectrum of the loaded trace"""
855        tau = self.fsZeroPadding + (np.max(self.fieldTimeV)-np.min(self.fieldTimeV))/2
856        self.fftFieldV = np.abs(self.fftFieldV)*np.exp(1.j*(2*np.pi*tau*self.frequencyAxis))
857        self.update_trace_from_fft()
858        self.strip_from_trace()
859        self.update_fft_spectrum()
860
861    def time_frequency_analysis(self, sigma_time, low_lim=None, up_lim=None, low_lim_freq=None, up_lim_freq=None):
862        """Performs time-frequency analysis by using scipy's short time fourier transform (fourier transform of the trace convoluted by a 'sigma_time' broad gaussian).
863
864        Args:
865            sigma_time: sigma of the gaussian window
866            low_lim, up_lim (float): xaxis limits for plotting. Default None
867            low_lim_freq, up_lim_freq (float): xaxis limits for plotting. Default None
868
869        """
870        dt = np.mean(np.diff(self.fieldTimeV))
871        w = scipy.signal.windows.gaussian(int(sigma_time / dt * 6) + 1, sigma_time / dt, sym=True)
872        TFA = scipy.signal.ShortTimeFFT(w, hop=1, fs=1. / dt, mfft=int(sigma_time / dt * 24), scale_to='magnitude')
873        TFData = TFA.stft(self.fieldV)
874
875        fig, ax = plt.subplots()
876        t_lo, t_hi, f_lo, f_hi = TFA.extent(self.fieldV.size)  # time and freq range of plot
877        if low_lim is None:
878            low_lim = t_lo+self.fieldTimeV[0]
879        if up_lim is None:
880            up_lim = t_hi+self.fieldTimeV[0]
881        if low_lim_freq is None:
882            low_lim_freq = 0
883        if up_lim_freq is None:
884            up_lim_freq = 3.0
885
886        ax.set( xlim=(low_lim, up_lim),
887                ylim=(low_lim_freq, up_lim_freq))
888        ax.set_xlabel('Time (fs)')
889        ax.set_ylabel('Frequency (PHz)')
890        im1 = ax.imshow(abs(TFData)/np.max(abs(TFData)), origin='lower', aspect='auto',
891                         extent=(t_lo+self.fieldTimeV[0], t_hi+self.fieldTimeV[0], f_lo, f_hi), cmap='viridis')
892        cbar = fig.colorbar(im1)
893
894        cbar.ax.set_ylabel("Magnitude of the field (Arb. unit)")
895        fig.tight_layout()
896        return TFData
897
898
899    def plot_trace(self, low_lim = None, up_lim = None, normalize: bool = True):
900        """Plots the field trace.
901
902        Args:
903            low_lim, up_lim: float = xaxis limits for plotting. Default None
904            normalize: bool = if True (default) normalize the peak of the trace to 1
905        """
906        fig, ax = plt.subplots()
907        if normalize:
908            norm_plot = self.normalization_trace
909        else:
910            norm_plot = 1
911        main_line = ax.plot(self.fieldTimeV, self.fieldV/norm_plot, label='Field trace')
912        if self.fieldStdevV is not None:
913            ax.fill_between(self.fieldTimeV, (self.fieldV - self.fieldStdevV)/norm_plot,
914                            (self.fieldV + self.fieldStdevV)/norm_plot, color=main_line[0].get_color(), alpha=0.3)
915        ax.set_xlabel('Time (fs)')
916        ax.set_ylabel('Field (Arb. unit)')
917
918        if low_lim is not None and up_lim is not None:
919            ax.set_xlim(low_lim, up_lim)
920        return fig
921
922    def plot_spectrum(self, low_lim = 40, up_lim = 1000, no_phase: bool = False, phase_blanking_level = 0.05):
923        """Plots the trace spectrum and phase together with the spectrometer measurement [if provided].
924
925        Args:
926            low_lim, up_lim (float): xaxis limits for plotting. Default: 40, 1000
927            no_phase: if True, don't plot the phase. Default: False
928        """
929        fig, ax = plt.subplots()
930
931        if not no_phase:
932            ax2 = ax.twinx()
933        lines = []
934        min_intensity = phase_blanking_level * np.max(self.fftSpectrum)
935        lines += ax.plot(self.wvlAxis[(self.wvlAxis>low_lim) & (self.wvlAxis<up_lim)], self.fftSpectrum[(self.wvlAxis>low_lim) & (self.wvlAxis<up_lim)],
936                label='Fourier transform')
937        if not no_phase:
938            ax2.plot([],[])
939            if self.wvlSpectrometer is not None:
940                ax2.plot([],[])
941            lines += ax2.plot(self.wvlAxis[(self.wvlAxis>low_lim)&(self.wvlAxis<up_lim)&(self.fftSpectrum>min_intensity)], self.fftphase[(self.wvlAxis>low_lim)&(self.wvlAxis<up_lim)&(self.fftSpectrum>min_intensity)],'--',
942                     label='Phase')
943        if self.wvlSpectrometer is not None:
944            lines += ax.plot(self.wvlSpectrometer[(self.wvlSpectrometer>low_lim)&(self.wvlSpectrometer<up_lim)], self.ISpectrometer[(self.wvlSpectrometer>low_lim)&(self.wvlSpectrometer<up_lim)],
945                    label='Spectrometer')
946        ax.set_xlabel('Wavelength (nm)')
947        ax.set_ylabel('Intensity (Arb. unit)')
948        ax.tick_params(axis='both')
949        if not no_phase:
950            ax2.set_ylabel('Phase (rad)')
951            ax2.tick_params(axis='y')
952        ax.legend(lines, [l.get_label() for l in lines])
953        return fig

Loads and stores the trace (field vs time) saved to file (two columns, tab separated) or given in the form of time and field [or wavelengths, spectrum and phase] arrays.

ALL THE TIMES ARE IN fs, FREQUENCIES IN PHz, WAVELENGTHS IN nm.

Most of the class methods modify the object data in place, and don't return anything.

Attributes:
  • fieldTimeV: (WAVEFORM DATA in the time domain) time array (fs)
  • fieldV: (WAVEFORM DATA in the time domain) field array
  • fieldStdevV: (WAVEFORM DATA in the time domain) field standard deviation (or sigma) array
  • frequencyAxis: (WAVEFORM DATA in the frequency domain) frequency axis of the FFT in PHz (should be np.fft compatible, i.e., equally spaced, in the form [0, df, 2*df, ..., fmax, -fmax[-df], ..., -df])
  • fftFieldV: (WAVEFORM DATA in the frequency domain) FFT field (complex)
  • complexFieldTimeV: (WAVEFORM DATA in the frequency domain) time axis of the complex field (fs)
  • complexFieldV: (WAVEFORM DATA in the frequency domain) complex field ( = IFFT{FFT(ω)θ(ω)}(t), where θ(ω) = 1 if ω >= 0, θ(ω) = 0 otherwise )
  • wvlAxis: (WAVEFORM DATA in the frequency domain) wavelength axis for the FFT spectrum (nm)
  • fftSpectrum: (WAVEFORM DATA in the frequency domain) wavelength-dependent positive FFT spectrum ( = |FFT{field}|^2 * df/dλ, λ > 0 )
  • fftphase: (WAVEFORM DATA in the frequency domain) wavelength-dependent spectral phase
  • wvlSpectrometer: (SPECTROMETER DATA) wavelength (nm)
  • ISpectrometer: (SPECTROMETER DATA) spectral intensity
  • fsZeroPadding: (= 150 by default) time span in fs for zero padding (appending zeroes both before and after the trace, in order to get a smoother fft)
  • filename: filename to load the trace from
  • filename_spectrum: filename to load the spectrum from
  • normalization_trace: normalization factor for the trace
  • zero_delay: time zero, corresponds to the maximum envelope
TraceHandler( filename=None, filename_spectrum=None, time=None, field=None, stdev=None, wvl=None, spectrum=None, wvl_FFT_trace=None, spectrum_FFT_trace=None, phase_FFT_trace=None)

136        """Constructor; loads the trace from file (or from time-field or wavelegth-spectrum-phase arrays) and stores it in the class.

138        One of the following must be provided (as a default all args are None):
139        * filename: the name of the file containing the trace (two columns, tab separated)
140        * time and field: the time vector (fs) and electric field vector (a.u.)
141        * wvl_FFT_trace, spectrum_FFT_trace and phase_FFT_trace: the wavelength (nm) spectrum (a.u.) and phase (rad) vectors
142
143        Args:
144            filename (str): the name of the file containing the trace (two columns - time and field, tab separated)
145            filename_spectrum (str): the name of the file containing the spectrum (two columns - wavelength and spectral intensity, tab separated)
146                this does not correspond to the fourier transform of the trace, but to some spectrometer data that you would like to compare to the loaded trace
147            time (array): the time vector (fs)
148            field (array): the electric field vector (a.u.)

150            wvl (array): the wavelength vector (nm) (spectrometer)
151            spectrum (array): the spectral intensity vector (a.u.) (spectrometer)
152            wvl_FFT_trace (array): the wavelength vector (nm) of the FFT trace (to reconstruct a trace from spectral data)
153            spectrum_FFT_trace (array): the spectral intensity vector (a.u.) of the FFT trace (to reconstruct a trace from spectral data)
154            phase_FFT_trace (array): the spectral phase vector (rad) of the FFT trace (to reconstruct a trace from spectral data)
155            """
156
157        self.fsZeroPadding = 150
158        self.filename = filename
159        self.filename_spectrum = filename_spectrum
160
161        self.fieldTimeV = None
162        self.fieldV = None
163        self.fieldStdevV = None

165        self.frequencyAxis = None
166        self.fftFieldV = None
167        self.complexFieldTimeV = None

170        self.fftSpectrum = None

173        self.wvlSpectrometer = None

181        elif time is not None and field is not None:

183        elif wvl_FFT_trace is not None and spectrum_FFT_trace is not None and phase_FFT_trace is not None:
184            self.load_trace_from_spectral_data(wvl_FFT_trace, spectrum_FFT_trace, phase_FFT_trace)
185        else:
186            print("\n\nWARNING: in function TraceHandler.__init__() no data was loaded\n\n")
187
188        if self.filename_spectrum is not None:
189            self.load_spectrum()
190        elif wvl is not None and spectrum is not None:
191            self.load_spectrum_from_arrays(wvl, spectrum)

loads from file

def load_trace_from_spectral_data(self, wvl_FFT_trace, spectrum_FFT_trace, phase_FFT_trace): 
238    def load_trace_from_spectral_data(self, wvl_FFT_trace, spectrum_FFT_trace, phase_FFT_trace):
239        """loads the trace from wavelength, spectrum, and spectral phase arrays and stores it in the class.
240
241        This function has a different job than load_spectrum_from_arrays(): in fact, it retrieves the trace from the given spectral data via fourier transform.
242
243        Args:
244            wvl_FFT_trace: wavelength array in nm
245            spectrum_FFT_trace: (wavelength-)spectral intensity array. This is assumed to be |FFT{field}|^2 * df/dλ
246            phase_FFT_trace: spectral phase in rad
247        """
248        check_equal_length(wvl_FFT_trace, spectrum_FFT_trace, phase_FFT_trace)
249
250        # check that the wvl_FFT_trace array is monotonically increasing
251        if np.any(np.diff(wvl_FFT_trace) < 0):
252            if np.all(np.diff(wvl_FFT_trace) < 0):
253                wvl_FFT_trace = wvl_FFT_trace[::-1]
254                spectrum_FFT_trace = spectrum_FFT_trace[::-1]
255                phase_FFT_trace = phase_FFT_trace[::-1]
256            else:
257                raise ValueError('in function TraceHandler.load_from_spectral_data() wavelength array is not monotonous')
258
259        # frequency spectrum (monotonically increasing)
260        freq = constants.speed_of_light / wvl_FFT_trace[::-1] * 1e-6
261        spectrum_freq = spectrum_FFT_trace[::-1] / (constants.speed_of_light/wvl_FFT_trace[::-1]**2 *1e-6)
262        phase_FFT_trace = phase_FFT_trace[::-1]
263
264        # create proper freq axis for the fourier transform
265        df = (freq[1]-freq[0])/4
266        nf = int(np.ceil(3 * freq[-1]/df))
267        self.frequencyAxis = np.concatenate((np.arange(0, nf), np.arange(-nf, 0))) * df
268        # corresponding time window
269        twin = 1./(df)
270
271        # complex fourier transform
272        spectrum_freq = np.sqrt(spectrum_freq)*np.exp(1.j*phase_FFT_trace)
273
274        # fill with zeros
275        initial_zero_freq = np.linspace(freq[1]-freq[0], freq[0], int(np.ceil(4 * freq[0]/(freq[1]-freq[0]))))
276        initial_zeros = np.zeros(len(initial_zero_freq))
277        final_zero_freq = np.linspace(2*freq[-1]-freq[-2], 4 * freq[-1], int(np.ceil(15 * freq[-1]/(freq[-1]-freq[-2]))))
278        final_zeros = np.zeros(len(final_zero_freq))
279        freq = np.concatenate((initial_zero_freq, freq, final_zero_freq))
280        spectrum_freq = np.concatenate((initial_zeros, spectrum_freq, final_zeros))
281        # add negative frequencies
282        freq = np.concatenate((-freq[::-1], freq))
283        spectrum_freq = np.concatenate((np.conjugate(spectrum_freq[::-1]), spectrum_freq))
284
285        # interpolate the spectrum to the frequency axis of the fft
286        self.fftFieldV = np.interp(self.frequencyAxis, freq, spectrum_freq)
287
288        # add linear phase to center the pulse in the time window; this has to be done after interpolation because the spectral phase will be fast oscillating
289        self.fftFieldV = self.fftFieldV*np.exp(1.j*2*np.pi*self.frequencyAxis*twin/2)
290
291        self.update_fft_spectrum()
292        self.update_trace_from_fft()

def update_fft(self, zero_pad_field=True): 
309    def update_fft(self, zero_pad_field = True):
310        """updates the fft of the trace from the time domain data.
311
312        Args:
313            zero_pad_field: bool; if true (default) add zeros before and after the trace before computing fft (for a smoother spectrum)
314                The length of appended zeros is defined by self.fsZeroPadding.
315        """
316        zp_fieldTimeV, zp_fieldV = deepcopy(self.fieldTimeV), deepcopy(self.fieldV)
317        if zero_pad_field:
318            zp_fieldTimeV, zp_fieldV = zero_padding(self.fieldTimeV, self.fieldV, fsExtension=self.fsZeroPadding)
319        self.frequencyAxis, self.fftFieldV = fourier_transform(zp_fieldTimeV, zp_fieldV)
320        self.update_fft_spectrum()

updates the fft of the trace from the time domain data.

Arguments:
  • zero_pad_field: bool; if true (default) add zeros before and after the trace before computing fft (for a smoother spectrum) The length of appended zeros is defined by self.fsZeroPadding.
def update_fft_spectrum(self): 
322    def update_fft_spectrum(self):
323        """Updates the wavelength-dependent intensity spectrum. Results are stored in self.wvlAxis and self.fftSpectrum.
324
325        This is (derived from but) different from the fourier transform because:
326         * it considers the squared modulus of the field
327         * it multiplies the frequency-dependent spectral density by df/dλ = c/λ²
328         * it considers only positive wavelengths
329
330        The function internally calls update_spectral_phase() as well.
331        """
332        self.wvlAxis = constants.speed_of_light/self.frequencyAxis[self.frequencyAxis > 0]*1.e-6
333        self.fftSpectrum = np.abs(self.fftFieldV[self.frequencyAxis > 0])**2 * constants.speed_of_light/self.wvlAxis**2
334        self.compute_complex_field()
335        self.update_spectral_phase()
336        self.normalize_fft_spectrum()

Updates the wavelength-dependent intensity spectrum. Results are stored in self.wvlAxis and self.fftSpectrum.

This is (derived from but) different from the fourier transform because:

  • it considers the squared modulus of the field
  • it multiplies the frequency-dependent spectral density by df/dλ = c/λ²
  • it considers only positive wavelengths

The function internally calls update_spectral_phase() as well.

def update_spectral_phase(self): 
338    def update_spectral_phase(self):
339        """computes the spectral phase of the trace. The result is stored in self.fftphase.
340
341        An attempt of automatic linear phase subtraction is made. Phase is unwrapped.
342        """
343        # determine the time distance (delay) of the waveform peak from the beginning of the trace (more precisely, from the beginning of the ifft)
344        tmax = self.get_zero_delay()
345        deltaT1 = tmax - self.complexFieldTimeV[0]
346        deltaT2 = self.complexFieldTimeV[-1] - tmax
347        ifft_twindow = 1/ (self.frequencyAxis[1] - self.frequencyAxis[0])
348        total_delay = ifft_twindow/2 + (deltaT2-deltaT1)/2 # total estimated delay of the peak from the beginning of the ifft trace
349
350        # compute the phase, use the computed 'delay' to correct for the non-interesting linear component, and unwrap it
351        self.fftphase = np.angle(self.fftFieldV[self.frequencyAxis > 0])
352        self.fftphase = self.fftphase - total_delay * self.frequencyAxis[self.frequencyAxis > 0] * 2 * np.pi
353        self.fftphase = np.unwrap(self.fftphase)
354
355        # subtract constant phase offset (m * 2*π)
356        n_pi =  np.sum(self.fftSpectrum*self.fftphase)/ np.sum(self.fftSpectrum)
357        n_pi = int( n_pi / ( 2*np.pi ))
358        self.fftphase -= n_pi * 2 * np.pi

computes the spectral phase of the trace. The result is stored in self.fftphase.

An attempt of automatic linear phase subtraction is made. Phase is unwrapped.

def strip_from_trace(self, timeRange=None): 
372    def strip_from_trace(self, timeRange = None):
373        """eliminates the zeros appended to the trace (zero-padding) when computing the FFT.
374
375        Useful when retrieving the trace via ifft (method update_trace_from_fft()).
376
377        Args:
378            timeRange (float): the time range (fs) to strip from the beginning and end of the trace. If None (default), fsZeroPadding is used.
379        """
380        if timeRange is None:
381            timeRange = self.fsZeroPadding
382        # strip the first and last fsZeroPadding time points
383        self.fieldV = self.fieldV[(self.fieldTimeV >= np.min(self.fieldTimeV) + timeRange)
384                                          & (self.fieldTimeV <= np.max(self.fieldTimeV) - timeRange)]
385        self.fieldTimeV = self.fieldTimeV[(self.fieldTimeV >= np.min(self.fieldTimeV) + timeRange)
386                                          & (self.fieldTimeV <= np.max(self.fieldTimeV) - timeRange)]
387        if self.fieldStdevV is None:
388            return True
389        if len(self.fieldStdevV) > len(self.fieldV):
390            n_remove = len(self.fieldStdevV)-len(self.fieldV)
391            print('\n\nWarning: fieldStdevV is longer than fieldV, removing', n_remove, ' elements\n\n')
392            while n_remove > 0:
393                if n_remove % 2 == 0:
394                    self.fieldStdevV = np.delete(self.fieldStdevV, 0)
395                else:
396                    self.fieldStdevV = np.delete(self.fieldStdevV, -1)
397                n_remove -= 1
398        elif len(self.fieldStdevV) < len(self.fieldV):
399            n_add = len(self.fieldV)-len(self.fieldStdevV)
400            print('\n\nWarning: fieldStdevV is shorter than fieldV, adding', n_add, ' elements\n\n')
401            while n_add > 0:
402                if n_add % 2 == 0:
403                    self.fieldStdevV = np.insert(self.fieldStdevV, 0, 0)
404                else:
405                    self.fieldStdevV = np.append(self.fieldStdevV, 0)
406                n_add -= 1
407        return True

def fourier_interpolation(self, ntimes_finer: int): 
430    def fourier_interpolation(self, ntimes_finer: int):
431        """Shrinks the time step of the trace in time domain by a factor ntimes_finer.
432
433        This is done by 'zero-padding' the fourier transform of the trace, i.e., by extending the frequency axis by a factor ntimes_finer, and adding corresponding zeros to the FFT field.
434
435        Args:
436            ntimes_finer (int): the factor by which to shrink the time step of the trace in time domain. Must be >= 1.
437        """
438        if ntimes_finer < 1:
439            raise ValueError('in function TraceHandler.fourier_interpolation() ntimes_finer must be >= 1')
440        if self.frequencyAxis is None or self.fftFieldV is None:
441            raise ValueError('in function TraceHandler.fourier_interpolation() frequency axis or fft field is not defined')
442        # extend the frequency axis by a factor ntimes_finer
443        df = self.frequencyAxis[1] - self.frequencyAxis[0]
444        i_last_pos = int(np.ceil(len(self.frequencyAxis) / 2) - 1)
445        if self.frequencyAxis[i_last_pos] < 0 or self.frequencyAxis[i_last_pos + 1] > 0:
446            print(self.frequencyAxis[0:i_last_pos + 1])
447            print(self.frequencyAxis[i_last_pos + 1:])
448            raise Exception('in function fourier_interpolation() frequency axes was not extended correctly')
449
450        appended_freqFFT = np.linspace(self.frequencyAxis[i_last_pos] + df, ntimes_finer * self.frequencyAxis[i_last_pos] + df,
451                                       round((ntimes_finer - 1) * self.frequencyAxis[i_last_pos] / df))
452        prepended_freqFFT = np.linspace(-(ntimes_finer - 1) * self.frequencyAxis[i_last_pos] + self.frequencyAxis[i_last_pos + 1],
453                                        +self.frequencyAxis[i_last_pos + 1], round((ntimes_finer - 1) * self.frequencyAxis[i_last_pos] / df))
454        self.frequencyAxis = np.concatenate(
455            (self.frequencyAxis[:i_last_pos + 1], appended_freqFFT, prepended_freqFFT, self.frequencyAxis[i_last_pos + 1:]))
456        self.fftFieldV = np.concatenate(
457            (self.fftFieldV[:i_last_pos + 1], np.zeros(len(appended_freqFFT)), np.zeros(len(prepended_freqFFT)),
458             self.fftFieldV[i_last_pos + 1:]))
459
460        self.update_trace_from_fft()
461        self.strip_from_trace()
462        self.update_fft_spectrum()

Shrinks the time step of the trace in time domain by a factor ntimes_finer.

This is done by 'zero-padding' the fourier transform of the trace, i.e., by extending the frequency axis by a factor ntimes_finer, and adding corresponding zeros to the FFT field.

Arguments:
  • ntimes_finer (int): the factor by which to shrink the time step of the trace in time domain. Must be >= 1.
def differentiate_trace(self, spectrally=True): 
464    def differentiate_trace(self, spectrally=True):
465        """computes the time derivative of the trace.
466
467        Args:
468            spectrally: bool; if True (default) the derivative will be computed in the spectral domain (maybe more stable numerically)

472            self.update_trace_from_fft()
473            self.update_fft_spectrum()
474        else:
475            self.fieldV = np.gradient(self.fieldV, self.fieldTimeV)
476            self.update_fft()

def integrate_trace(self, spectrally=True): 
478    def integrate_trace(self, spectrally=True):
479        """integrates the trace in time.
480
481        Args:
482            spectrally (bool): if True (default) the integral will be computed in the spectral domain (maybe more stable numerically)
483        """
484        if spectrally:
485            if self.frequencyAxis[0] != 0:
486                print('WARNING: in function TraceHandler.integrate_trace() the FFT axis\' first element is not zero')
487            self.fftFieldV[1:] = -1j / self.frequencyAxis[1:] * self.fftFieldV[1:]
488            self.update_trace_from_fft()
489            self.update_fft_spectrum()
490        else:
491            self.fieldV = np.cumsum(self.fieldV) * np.mean(np.diff(self.fieldTimeV))
492            self.update_fft()

def normalize_spectrum(self): 
510    def normalize_spectrum(self):
511        """Normalizes the comparison spectrum to its integral."""
512        spectrum_range = [60, 930]
513        n_factor = (np.abs(np.diff(self.wvlSpectrometer)[(self.wvlSpectrometer[:-1] > spectrum_range[0]) & (
514                    self.wvlSpectrometer[:-1] < spectrum_range[1])]) *
515                               self.ISpectrometer[:-1][(self.wvlSpectrometer[:-1] > spectrum_range[0]) & (
516                                       self.wvlSpectrometer[:-1] < spectrum_range[1])]).sum()
517        self.ISpectrometer /= n_factor

def normalize_fft_spectrum(self, spectrum_range=[60, 930]): 
519    def normalize_fft_spectrum(self, spectrum_range = [60, 930]):
520        """Normalizes the spectrum of the trace (|FFT{trace}|^2 * df/dλ) to its integral (area)
521
522        Args:
523            spectrum_range (list): the range of wavelengths (nm) to consider for the normalization. Default is [60, 930] nm.
524        """
525        n_factor = (np.abs(np.diff(self.wvlAxis)[(self.wvlAxis[:-1] > spectrum_range[0]) & (
526                    self.wvlAxis[:-1] < spectrum_range[1])]) *
527                               self.fftSpectrum[:-1][(self.wvlAxis[:-1] > spectrum_range[0]) & (
528                                       self.wvlAxis[:-1] < spectrum_range[1])]).sum()
529        self.fftSpectrum /= n_factor

def get_positive_fft_field(self): 
547    def get_positive_fft_field(self):
548        """Returns the positive frequency axis f and the corresponding FFT field (complex).
549
550        Main task of this function is to 'smooth' the phase of the fft (= remove linear phase, corresponding to a time shift in the temporal domain), since the waveform is usually centered around t = 0"""
551        if self.frequencyAxis is None or self.fftFieldV is None:
552            raise ValueError('in function TraceHandler.get_positive_fft_field() frequency axis or fft field is not defined')
553        positive_freq = self.frequencyAxis[self.frequencyAxis >= 0]
554        positive_fft_field = self.fftFieldV[self.frequencyAxis >= 0]
555        # remove linear phase
556        tmax = self.get_zero_delay()
557        deltaT1 = tmax - self.fieldTimeV[0]
558        deltaT2 = self.fieldTimeV[-1] - tmax
559        ifft_twindow = 1 / (self.frequencyAxis[1] - self.frequencyAxis[0])
560        total_delay = ifft_twindow / 2 + (deltaT2 - deltaT1) / 2
561        positive_fft_field = positive_fft_field * np.exp(-1.j * 2 * np.pi * positive_freq * total_delay)
562        return positive_freq, positive_fft_field

Returns the positive frequency axis f and the corresponding FFT field (complex).

588    def compute_complex_field(self):
589        """Computes the complex trace by inverting the positive-freq FFT and stores it in self.complexFieldV (for envelope or phase computation, for example)

596        self.strip_from_complex_trace()
