def fft_tukey_bandpass( self, lowWavelengthEdge, upWavelengthEdge, lowEdgeWidth, highEdgeWidth): 
647    def fft_tukey_bandpass(self, lowWavelengthEdge, upWavelengthEdge, lowEdgeWidth, highEdgeWidth):
648        """Applies a bandpass filter to the trace in the frequency domain using a tukey window.
649
650        The tukey window is 1 between  lowWavelengthEdge+lowEdgeWidth/2  and  upWavelengthEdge-highEdgeWidth/2
651        and it is reaches zero at lowWavelengthEdge-lowEdgeWidth/2  and  upWavelengthEdge+highEdgeWidth/2.
652        Notice that the edges are only cosine-shaped in the frequency domain. In the wavelength domain upWavelengthEdge - lowWavelengthEdge does not coincide with the FWHM of the tukey function
653
654        Args:
655            lowWavelengthEdge: float (nm)
656            upWavelengthEdge: float (nm)
657            lowEdgeWidth: float (nm)
658            highEdgeWidth: float (nm)
659        """
660        upFreqEdge = constants.speed_of_light / (lowWavelengthEdge - lowEdgeWidth / 2) /2 * 1e-6 + constants.speed_of_light / (
661                    lowWavelengthEdge + lowEdgeWidth / 2) /2 * 1e-6
662        lowFreqEdge = constants.speed_of_light / (upWavelengthEdge - highEdgeWidth / 2) /2 * 1e-6 + constants.speed_of_light / (
663                    upWavelengthEdge + highEdgeWidth / 2) /2 * 1e-6
664
665        upFreqEdgeWidth = constants.speed_of_light / (lowWavelengthEdge - lowEdgeWidth / 2) * 1e-6 - constants.speed_of_light / (
666                    lowWavelengthEdge + lowEdgeWidth / 2) * 1e-6
667        lowFreqEdgeWidth = constants.speed_of_light / (upWavelengthEdge - highEdgeWidth / 2) * 1e-6 - constants.speed_of_light / (
668                    upWavelengthEdge + highEdgeWidth / 2) * 1e-6
669
670        window = asymmetric_tukey_window(np.abs(self.frequencyAxis), lowFreqEdge, upFreqEdge, lowFreqEdgeWidth,
671                                         upFreqEdgeWidth)
672        self.fftFieldV = self.fftFieldV * window
673        self.update_trace_from_fft()
674        self.update_fft_spectrum()
675        self.strip_from_trace()

Applies a bandpass filter to the trace in the frequency domain using a tukey window.

The tukey window is 1 between lowWavelengthEdge+lowEdgeWidth/2 and upWavelengthEdge-highEdgeWidth/2 and it is reaches zero at lowWavelengthEdge-lowEdgeWidth/2 and upWavelengthEdge+highEdgeWidth/2. Notice that the edges are only cosine-shaped in the frequency domain. In the wavelength domain upWavelengthEdge - lowWavelengthEdge does not coincide with the FWHM of the tukey function

Arguments:
  • lowWavelengthEdge: float (nm)
  • upWavelengthEdge: float (nm)
  • lowEdgeWidth: float (nm)
  • highEdgeWidth: float (nm)
def apply_transmission(self, wavelengths, f): 
677    def apply_transmission(self, wavelengths, f):
678        """Applies a spectral transmission function to the trace (e.g. spectral filter).
679
680        Args:
681            wavelengths: ndarray = wavelength array (nm)
682            f: ndarray = transmission function f(λ)
683        """
684        if np.any(np.diff(wavelengths)) < 0:
685            if np.all(np.diff(wavelengths)) < 0:
686                wavelengths = wavelengths[::-1]
687                f = f[::-1]
688            else:
689                raise ValueError('in function TraceHandler.apply_transmission() wavelength array is not monotonous')
690        freq = constants.speed_of_light / wavelengths[::-1] * 1e-6
691        spectrum_freq = f[::-1]
692
693        # fill with zeros
694        initial_zero_freq = np.linspace(freq[1]-freq[0], freq[0], int(np.ceil(4 * freq[0]/(freq[1]-freq[0]))))
695        initial_zeros = np.zeros(len(initial_zero_freq))
696        final_zero_freq = np.linspace(2*freq[-1]-freq[-2], 4 * freq[-1], int(np.ceil(15 * freq[-1]/(freq[-1]-freq[-2]))))
697        final_zeros = np.zeros(len(final_zero_freq))
698        freq = np.concatenate((initial_zero_freq, freq, final_zero_freq))
699        spectrum_freq = np.concatenate((initial_zeros, spectrum_freq, final_zeros))
700        # add negative frequencies
701        freq = np.concatenate((-freq[::-1], freq))
702        spectrum_freq = np.concatenate((spectrum_freq[::-1], spectrum_freq))
703
704        #interpolate the spectrum to the frequency axis of the fft
705        spectrum_interp = np.interp(self.frequencyAxis, freq, spectrum_freq)
706
707        self.fftFieldV = self.fftFieldV * spectrum_interp
708        self.update_trace_from_fft()
709        self.update_fft_spectrum()
710        self.strip_from_trace()

Applies a spectral transmission function to the trace (e.g. spectral filter).

Arguments:
  • wavelengths: ndarray = wavelength array (nm)
  • f: ndarray = transmission function f(λ)
def apply_spectrum( self, wvl=None, spectrum=None, CEP_shift: float = 0.0, stripZeroPadding: bool = True): 
712    def apply_spectrum(self, wvl = None , spectrum = None, CEP_shift: float = 0., stripZeroPadding: bool = True):
713        """Applies a spectrum to the phase of the trace. This means that a new trace is computed and stored in the TraceHandler object (replacing the existing one);
714        the new trace has spectral intensity equal to the applied spectrum and spectral phase equal to the phase of the existing trace.
715
716        Args:
717            wvl: wavelength array (nm). If None (default) the comparison spectrum stored in the class (self.wvlSpectrometer and self.ISpectrometer) is applied.
718            spectrum: spectral intensity array. If None (default) the comparison spectrum stored in the class (self.wvlSpectrometer and self.ISpectrometer) is applied.
719            CEP_shift: a possible artificial phase shift IN UNITS OF PI! (default = 0)
720            stripZeroPadding (bool): whether to eliminate the zero padding (zeros appended to the trace). Default is True"""
721
722        if wvl is None or spectrum is None:
723            wvl = self.wvlSpectrometer
724            spectrum = self.ISpectrometer
725        # check that the wvl array is monotonically increasing
726        if np.any(np.diff(wvl) < 0):
727            if np.all(np.diff(wvl) < 0):
728                wvl = wvl[::-1]
729                spectrum = spectrum[::-1]
730            else:
731                raise ValueError('in function TraceHandler.apply_spectrum() wavelength array is not monotonous')
732
733        # frequency spectrum (monotonically increasing)
734        freq = constants.speed_of_light / wvl[::-1] *1e-6
735        spectrum_freq = spectrum[::-1] / (constants.speed_of_light/wvl[::-1]**2 *1e-6)
736        spectrum_freq = np.maximum(spectrum_freq, np.zeros(len(spectrum_freq)))
737
738        # fill with zeros
739        initial_zero_freq = np.linspace(freq[1]-freq[0], freq[0], int(np.ceil(4 * freq[0]/(freq[1]-freq[0]))))
740        initial_zeros = np.zeros(len(initial_zero_freq))
741        final_zero_freq = np.linspace(2*freq[-1]-freq[-2], 4 * freq[-1], int(np.ceil(15 * freq[-1]/(freq[-1]-freq[-2]))))
742        final_zeros = np.zeros(len(final_zero_freq))
743        freq = np.concatenate((initial_zero_freq, freq, final_zero_freq))
744        spectrum_freq = np.concatenate((initial_zeros, spectrum_freq, final_zeros))
745        # add negative frequencies
746        freq = np.concatenate((-freq[::-1], freq))
747        spectrum_freq = np.concatenate((spectrum_freq[::-1], spectrum_freq))
748
749        # interpolate the spectrum to the frequency axis of the fft
750        spectrum_interp = np.interp(self.frequencyAxis, freq, spectrum_freq)
751        self.fftFieldV = np.sqrt(spectrum_interp)*np.exp(1j*np.angle(self.fftFieldV) + 1j*np.pi*CEP_shift*np.sign(self.frequencyAxis))
752
753
754        self.update_trace_from_fft()
755        if stripZeroPadding:
756            self.strip_from_trace()
757        else:
758            self.fieldStdevV = None
759        self.update_fft_spectrum()

Arguments:

  • spectrum: spectral intensity array. If None (default) the comparison spectrum stored in the class (self.wvlSpectrometer and self.ISpectrometer) is applied.
  • CEP_shift: a possible artificial phase shift IN UNITS OF PI! (default = 0)
  • stripZeroPadding (bool): whether to eliminate the zero padding (zeros appended to the trace). Default is True
def fresnel_reflection( self, material2, angle_in, material1=None, forward: bool = True, s_polarized: bool = True, path: str = './RefractiveIndices/'): 
761    def fresnel_reflection(self, material2, angle_in, material1=None, forward: bool=True, s_polarized: bool=True, path: str = "./RefractiveIndices/"):
762        """calculates the fresnel reflection of the pulse at the interface between two materials. The waveform is travelling from material 1 to material 2.
763        The first medium (material1) should be non-absorptive. As usual the resulting waveform is stored in the TraceHandler object, replacing the previous one.
764
765        Refractive index files should contain 3 space-separated columns, respectively with headers: wvl n k, where wvl is the wavelength in um, n and k resp. the real and imaginary part of the refractive index.
766        Args:
767            material2: the filename (without '.txt') of the refractive index data for the material after the interface (e.g. Si Al MgF2); wavelength is in um in the refractive index file
768            angle_in: the incidence angle in degrees
769            material1: the filename (without '.txt') of the refractive index data for the material before the interface. If None (default), vacuum is assumed
770            forward (bool):  if True (default) forward reflection is computed (the result waveform is the reflection of the previously stored waveform.
771
772                if False backward reflection is computed (the previous waveform is the reflection of the result waveform)
773            s_polarized (bool): True. Reflection calculation only implemented for s-polarized light
774            path (str): path for the refractive index files. Defaults to "./RefractiveIndices/"
775            """
776        if not s_polarized:
777            raise ValueError('in function TraceHandler.fresnel_reflection() p_polarized is not implemented yet\n')
778
779        # read refractive index
780        refIndexData = pandas.read_table(path + material2 + ".txt", sep=" ", keep_default_na=False)
781        wvl2 = np.array(refIndexData['wvl']) * 1e3
782        n2 = np.array(refIndexData['n']) +1j* np.array(refIndexData['k'])
783        if material1 is None:
784            wvl1 = np.array(wvl2)
785            n1 = n2*0 + 1
786        else:
787            refIndexData = pandas.read_table(path + material1 + ".txt", sep=" ", keep_default_na=False)
788            wvl1 = np.array(refIndexData['wvl']) * 1e3
789            n1 = np.array(refIndexData['n']) +1j* np.array(refIndexData['k'])
790
791        # check that the wvl arrays are monotonically increasing
792        if np.any(np.diff(wvl1) < 0):
793            if np.all(np.diff(wvl1) < 0):
794                wvl1 = wvl1[::-1]
795                n1 = n1[::-1]
796            else:
797                raise ValueError('in function TraceHandler.fresnel_reflection() wavelength array is not monotonous')
798        if np.any(np.diff(wvl2) < 0):
799            if np.all(np.diff(wvl2) < 0):
800                wvl2 = wvl2[::-1]
801                n2 = n2[::-1]
802            else:
803                raise ValueError('in function TraceHandler.fresnel_reflection() wavelength array is not monotonous')
804
805        # frequency spectrum (monotonically increasing)
806        freq1 = constants.speed_of_light / wvl1[::-1] * 1e-6
807        freq2 = constants.speed_of_light / wvl2[::-1] * 1e-6
808        n1 = n1[::-1]
809        n2 = n2[::-1]
810
811        # fill with ones
812        initial_ones_freq = np.linspace(freq1[1] - freq1[0], freq1[0], int(np.ceil(4 * freq1[0] / (freq1[1] - freq1[0]))))
813        initial_ones = np.ones(len(initial_ones_freq)) * n1[0]
814        final_ones_freq = np.linspace(2 * freq1[-1] - freq1[-2], 4 * freq1[-1],
815                                      int(np.ceil(15 * freq1[-1] / (freq1[-1] - freq1[-2]))))
816        final_ones = np.ones(len(final_ones_freq)) * n1[-1]
817        freq1 = np.concatenate((initial_ones_freq, freq1, final_ones_freq))
818        n1 = np.concatenate((initial_ones, n1, final_ones))
819        # same for n2
820        initial_ones_freq = np.linspace(freq2[1] - freq2[0], freq2[0], int(np.ceil(4 * freq2[0] / (freq2[1] - freq2[0]))))
821        initial_ones = np.ones(len(initial_ones_freq))* n2[0]
822        final_ones_freq = np.linspace(2 * freq2[-1] - freq2[-2], 4 * freq2[-1],
823                                        int(np.ceil(15 * freq2[-1] / (freq2[-1] - freq2[-2]))))
824        final_ones = np.ones(len(final_ones_freq)) * n2[-1]
825        freq2 = np.concatenate((initial_ones_freq, freq2, final_ones_freq))
826        n2 = np.concatenate((initial_ones, n2, final_ones))
827
828        # add negative frequencies
829        freq1 = np.concatenate((-freq1[::-1], freq1))
830        n1 = np.concatenate((np.conjugate(n1[::-1]), n1))
831        freq2 = np.concatenate((-freq2[::-1], freq2))
832        n2 = np.concatenate((np.conjugate(n2[::-1]), n2))
833
834        # interpolate the n1 and n2 to the frequency axis of the fft
835        n1Interp = np.interp(self.frequencyAxis, freq1, n1)
836        n2Interp = np.interp(self.frequencyAxis, freq2, n2)
837
838        # calculate the fresnel reflection coefficients using only the angle of incidence (NOT SURE THIS WORKS WHEN THE FIRST MEDIUM IS LOSSY)
839        r = ((n1Interp * np.cos(angle_in*np.pi/180) - n2Interp * np.sqrt(1-(n1Interp/n2Interp*np.sin(angle_in*np.pi/180))**2)) /
840             (n1Interp * np.cos(angle_in*np.pi/180) + n2Interp * np.sqrt(1-(n1Interp/n2Interp*np.sin(angle_in*np.pi/180))**2)))
841        if forward:
842            self.fftFieldV = self.fftFieldV * r
843        else:
844            self.fftFieldV = self.fftFieldV / r
845
846        self.fieldStdevV = None
847
848        self.update_trace_from_fft()
849        self.strip_from_trace()
850        self.update_fft_spectrum()

def apply_zero_phase(self): 
853    def apply_zero_phase(self):
854        """Applies zero-phase to the trace; this allows, for example, to retrieve the fourier limited pulse corresponding to the same FFT spectrum of the loaded trace"""
855        tau = self.fsZeroPadding + (np.max(self.fieldTimeV)-np.min(self.fieldTimeV))/2
856        self.fftFieldV = np.abs(self.fftFieldV)*np.exp(1.j*(2*np.pi*tau*self.frequencyAxis))
857        self.update_trace_from_fft()
858        self.strip_from_trace()
859        self.update_fft_spectrum()

def time_frequency_analysis( self, sigma_time, low_lim=None, up_lim=None, low_lim_freq=None, up_lim_freq=None): 
861    def time_frequency_analysis(self, sigma_time, low_lim=None, up_lim=None, low_lim_freq=None, up_lim_freq=None):
862        """Performs time-frequency analysis by using scipy's short time fourier transform (fourier transform of the trace convoluted by a 'sigma_time' broad gaussian).
863
864        Args:
865            sigma_time: sigma of the gaussian window
866            low_lim, up_lim (float): xaxis limits for plotting. Default None
867            low_lim_freq, up_lim_freq (float): xaxis limits for plotting. Default None
868
869        """
870        dt = np.mean(np.diff(self.fieldTimeV))
871        w = scipy.signal.windows.gaussian(int(sigma_time / dt * 6) + 1, sigma_time / dt, sym=True)
872        TFA = scipy.signal.ShortTimeFFT(w, hop=1, fs=1. / dt, mfft=int(sigma_time / dt * 24), scale_to='magnitude')
873        TFData = TFA.stft(self.fieldV)
874
875        fig, ax = plt.subplots()
876        t_lo, t_hi, f_lo, f_hi = TFA.extent(self.fieldV.size)  # time and freq range of plot
877        if low_lim is None:
878            low_lim = t_lo+self.fieldTimeV[0]
879        if up_lim is None:
880            up_lim = t_hi+self.fieldTimeV[0]
881        if low_lim_freq is None:
882            low_lim_freq = 0
883        if up_lim_freq is None:
884            up_lim_freq = 3.0
885
886        ax.set( xlim=(low_lim, up_lim),
887                ylim=(low_lim_freq, up_lim_freq))
888        ax.set_xlabel('Time (fs)')
889        ax.set_ylabel('Frequency (PHz)')
890        im1 = ax.imshow(abs(TFData)/np.max(abs(TFData)), origin='lower', aspect='auto',
891                         extent=(t_lo+self.fieldTimeV[0], t_hi+self.fieldTimeV[0], f_lo, f_hi), cmap='viridis')
892        cbar = fig.colorbar(im1)
893
894        cbar.ax.set_ylabel("Magnitude of the field (Arb. unit)")
895        fig.tight_layout()
896        return TFData

def tukey_f(x: float, center: float, FWHM: float, w: float): 
43def tukey_f(x: float, center: float, FWHM: float, w: float):
44    """cosine-smoothed, flattop window function centered in 'center'
45
46    each edge is w-wide
47    amplitude = 1
48
49    ARGUMENTS:
50        x: float = input value
51        center = center of the t. function
52        FWHM = full width at half maximum of the t. function
53        w = width of the edges of the t. function (0 < w < FWHM)
54        """
55    if FWHM < w:
56        print('tukey window can not have edges wider than FWHM')
57        pass
58    xmin = center - FWHM/2 - w/2
59    xmax = center + FWHM/2 + w/2
60    if x < xmin or x > xmax:
61        y = 0
62    elif xmin <= x and x < xmin + w:
63        y = (1-np.cos((x-xmin)*np.pi/w))/2
64    elif xmin + w <= x and x <= xmax - w:
65        y = 1
66    elif xmax - w < x and x <= xmax:
67        y = (1-np.cos((x-xmax)*np.pi/w))/2
68    else:
69        print (x, xmax, xmin, w)
70        raise ValueError('in tukey_f, x could not be assigned correctly to the sub intervals, might it (or the other parameters) be NaN?')
71    return y

cosine-smoothed, flattop window function centered in 'center'

each edge is w-wide amplitude = 1

ARGUMENTS:

x: float = input value center = center of the t. function FWHM = full width at half maximum of the t. function w = width of the edges of the t. function (0 < w < FWHM)

def tukey_window(x, center: float, FWHM: float, w: float): 
73def tukey_window(x, center: float, FWHM: float, w: float):
74    """returns a cosine-smoothed, flattop window centered in 'center'; amplitude = 1.
75
76    The difference with the function tukey_f is that this function can take as input a numpy array or a list, and returns a numpy array or a list.
77
78    Args:
79        x: input array (numpy array or list)
80        center: center of the window
81        FWHM: full width at half maximum
82        w: width of the edges of the window (w > 0)
83
84    Returns:
85        window (numpy array or list)"""
86    if isinstance(x, np.ndarray):
87        y = []
88        for xi in x:
89            y.append(tukey_f(xi, center, FWHM, w))
90        y = np.array(y)
91    elif isinstance(x, list):
92        y = []
93        for xi in x:
94            y.append(tukey_f(xi, center, FWHM, w))
95    elif isinstance(x, float):
96        y = tukey_f(x, center, FWHM, w)
97    else:
98        raise TypeError('in function tukey window x is neither np array nor list nor float')
99    return y

def read_spectrometer_excel(filename): 
152def read_spectrometer_excel(filename):
153    """Reads xls file (passed as the string filename without extension!) produced by the UV-VIS spectrometer RESONANCE VS-7550-VUV.
154
155        This function currently only works in Linux (Ubuntu), since it uses the OS system command to brutally copy the content of the xls file into a txt;
156        such copying is necessary because the xls file is not readable by pandas (it's a non-standard xls, I couldn't find any other workaround).
157        For windows there is a similar command, please replace the line
158        os.system("cat " + filename + ".xls > " + filename + ".txt")
159
160        44 (skipped) rows at the beginning of the file (all headers)
161
162        Args:
163            filename: name of the file (without extension)
164
165        Returns:
166            numpy array with the spectral data (see original excel for more details)"""
167    if '.' in filename and './' not in filename:
168        raise ValueError('in function read_spectrometer_excel, filename must be passed without extension (filename should not contain a dot)')
169    os.system("cat " + filename + ".xls > " + filename + ".txt")
170    dataF = pandas.read_table(filename + ".txt", sep='\t', keep_default_na=False, skiprows=44)  # keep_default_na=False,
171    data = []
172    for row in dataF.values:
173        data.append([])
174        for x in row:
175            if x == '':
176                data[-1].append(float('nan'))
177            else:
178                data[-1].append(float(x))
179    return np.array(data)

188        calibration_file_path: path of the calibration file
189        dark: dark spectrum (optional)
190        dark_c: column of the dark spectrum (optional)
191        stitch: Boolean, if True, the spectra are stitched together (optional, default False)
192                if True, the spectrum will be calculated by stitching the 5 partial spectra in the previous columns.
193                the stitching only works if the spectrum number 'column' is a FULL-SPECTRUM in the xls file.
194                Stitching was implemented because the internal software of the spectrometer is not good enough at it (the saved full spectrum typically has discontinuities).
195        smooth_points: number of points for smoothing (optional, default 10). if 0, no smoothing is applied
196        null_calibration: Boolean, if True, the intensity calibration is not applied (optional, default False)
197        wavelength_calibration_intercept: intercept of the wavelength calibration (optional, default 3.538). If None no wavelength calibration is applied
198        wavelength_calibration_slope: slope of the wavelength calibration (optional, default 1.003427). If None no wavelength calibration is applied
199                Wavelength calibration is in the form λ_true = λ_measured * slope + intercept
200                Notice: wavelength calibration has an error of +/- 1  to 2 nm due to the stitching process.
201                    for a better calibration compute and apply the correction to each of the 5 partial spectra
202
203    Returns:
204        wavelength: wavelength array
205        spectrum: calibrated spectrum
206    """
207    wavelength_calibration, lamp_spec, lamp_measbyReso, calibration_smoothed = load_calibration_data(calibration_file_path)
208
209    if wavelength_calibration_slope is None or wavelength_calibration_intercept is None:
210        cal_slope = 1.
211        cal_intercept = 0.
212    else:
213        cal_slope = wavelength_calibration_slope
214        cal_intercept = wavelength_calibration_intercept
215
216    if stitch:
217        # check that the chosen spectrum (in column) is actually a full one
218        theoretically_complete_wvl = data[:, 7 * (column) + 1]*cal_slope + cal_intercept
219        theoretically_complete_wvl = theoretically_complete_wvl[~np.isnan(theoretically_complete_wvl)]
220        if theoretically_complete_wvl[-1]-theoretically_complete_wvl[0] < 900:
221            raise ValueError('in function calibrate(), the spectrum to be stitched is not a full spectrum, please check the column index')
222
223        extrema = []
224        spectra = []
225        for i in range(5):
226            wvl_single_sp = data[:, 7 * (column - 5 + i) + 1]*cal_slope + cal_intercept
227            single_sp = data[:, 7 * (column - 5 + i) + 2]
228            if dark is not None and dark_c is not None:
229                single_sp -= dark[:, 7 * (dark_c -5 +i) +2]
230            wvl_single_sp = wvl_single_sp[~np.isnan(wvl_single_sp)]
231            single_sp = single_sp[~np.isnan(single_sp)]
232            extrema.append([wvl_single_sp[0], wvl_single_sp[-1]])
233            spectra.append([wvl_single_sp, single_sp])
234
235        overlaps = []
236        centers_of_overlap = [extrema[0][0]]
237        for i in range(4):
238            overlaps.append(extrema[i][1] - extrema[i+1][0])
239            centers_of_overlap.append(extrema[i][1]/2 + extrema[i+1][0]/2)
240
241        w = np.min(overlaps)
242        centers_of_overlap.append(extrema[4][1]+w/2)
243        centers_of_overlap[0] = centers_of_overlap[0]-w/2
244
245        wavelength = data[:, 7*column +1]*cal_slope + cal_intercept
246        spectrum = wavelength * 0.
247
248        for i in range(5):
249            center = centers_of_overlap[i]/2+centers_of_overlap[i+1]/2
250            FWHM = centers_of_overlap[i+1] - centers_of_overlap[i]
251            spectrum += np.interp(wavelength, spectra[i][0], spectra[i][1]*tukey_window(spectra[i][0], center, FWHM, w))
252            plt.plot(spectra[i][0], spectra[i][1]*tukey_window(spectra[i][0], center, FWHM, w))
253        calibr_interpolated = np.interp(wavelength, wavelength_calibration, calibration_smoothed)
254        if not null_calibration:
255            spectrum *= calibr_interpolated
256
257        plt.plot(data[:, 7*column +1]*cal_slope+cal_intercept, data[:, 7*column +2])
258        plt.plot(wavelength, spectrum)
259
260        if w < 0:
261            raise ValueError('in function calibrate(), the spectra to be stitched do not overlap')
262
263    else:
264        wavelength = data[:, 7*column +1]*cal_slope + cal_intercept
265        if dark is None or dark_c is None:
266            calibr_interpolated = np.interp(wavelength, wavelength_calibration, calibration_smoothed)
267            if null_calibration:
268                calibr_interpolated = calibr_interpolated*0. +1
269            spectrum = (data[:, 7*column +2] - np.min(data[:, 7*column +2]))*calibr_interpolated
270        else:
271            calibr_interpolated = np.interp(wavelength, wavelength_calibration, calibration_smoothed)
272            if null_calibration:
273                calibr_interpolated = calibr_interpolated*0. +1
274            spectrum = (data[:, 7*column +2] - dark[:, 7*dark_c +2])*calibr_interpolated
275
276            if len(data[:, 7*column +2][~np.isnan(data[:, 7*column +2])]) != len(dark[:, 7*dark_c +2][~np.isnan(dark[:, 7*dark_c +2])]):
277                raise ValueError('In function calibrate(), the dark spectrum is not the same length as the spectrum to be calibrated.\n'
278                                 'Please check the column indices of the dark spectrum and the main spectrum')
279            if data[:, 7*column +1][~np.isnan(data[:, 7*column +1])][0] != dark[:, 7*dark_c +2][~np.isnan(dark[:, 7*dark_c +1])][0]:
280                print('WARNING: In function calibrate(), the dark spectrum does not have the same wavelength as the spectrum to be calibrated.\n'
281                                 'Please check the column indices of the dark spectrum and the main spectrum')
282
283    if smooth_points is not None and smooth_points > 0:
284        spectrum = smooth(spectrum, smooth_points)
285    return wavelength, spectrum

def eliminate_outliers(y, threshold: float = 3, window_points: int = 20): 
12def eliminate_outliers(y, threshold: float=3, window_points: int=20):
13    """Eliminates outliers in the data by replacing them with the mean of the surrounding values.
14
15    Args:
16        y (np.ndarray): Input data array.
17        threshold (float): Threshold in units of sigma for outlier detection. Default is 3.
18        window_points (int): Number of points to consider for the mean and sigma calculation. Default is 20.
19    """
20    if not isinstance(y, np.ndarray):
21        raise TypeError("Input of eliminate_outliers must be a numpy array.")
22    n_outliers = 0
23    for i in range(len(y)):
24        window_lower = int(max(0, i - window_points/2))
25        window_upper = int(min(len(y), i + window_points/2))
26        mean = np.mean(y[window_lower:window_upper])
27        std = np.std(y[window_lower:window_upper])
28        if abs(y[i] - mean) > threshold * std:
29            y[i] = np.mean(np.concatenate((y[window_lower:i], y[i+1:window_upper])))
30            n_outliers += 1
31
32    print(n_outliers, " outliers detected and replaced with mean of surrounding values.")

Eliminates outliers in the data by replacing them with the mean of the surrounding values.

Arguments:
  • y (np.ndarray): Input data array.
  • threshold (float): Threshold in units of sigma for outlier detection. Default is 3.
  • window_points (int): Number of points to consider for the mean and sigma calculation. Default is 20.
def read_spectrum_maya( filename, remove_offsets_individually=False, nm_smearing=1.0, eliminate_outliers_spectrum=False): 
34def read_spectrum_maya(filename, remove_offsets_individually=False, nm_smearing=1., eliminate_outliers_spectrum=False):
35    """Reads a spectrum file from the Maya spectrometer and returns the wavelength and spectrum arrays.
36
37    The file is expected to have one column of wavelength data and arbitrarily many columns of equivalent spectra [to be averaged].
38    The function also applies a Gaussian filter to the spectrum data to smooth it.
39    The function can optionally eliminate outliers in the spectrum data and remove offsets from each column individually.
40
41    Args:
42        filename
43        remove_offsets_individually (bool): If True, compute and remove offsets from each column individually
44        nm_smearing (float): sigma in nm of the gaussian filter applied to smooth the spectrum.
45        eliminate_outliers_spectrum (bool): = If True, eliminate single pixel outliers in the spectral data and replace them with average of surrounding values.
46            default is False.
47        """
48    data = pandas.read_table(filename, sep=' ', keep_default_na=True, skiprows=0)
49    spectrum = []
50    offsets = [0.]*len(data.columns)
51    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
52    wvl = np.array(data.iloc[:, 0])
53    final_nm_smearing = nm_smearing
54    if eliminate_outliers_spectrum:
55        nm_smearing = 0
56    for i in range(len(data.columns)-1):
57        if nm_smearing > 0:
58            spectrum_i = gaussian_filter1d(np.array(data.iloc[:, i+1]), sigma=nm_smearing/(wvl[1]-wvl[0]))
59        else:
60            spectrum_i = np.array(data.iloc[:, i+1])
61        if eliminate_outliers_spectrum:
62            eliminate_outliers(spectrum_i, threshold=3, window_points=20)
63            spectrum_i = gaussian_filter1d(spectrum_i, sigma=final_nm_smearing/(wvl[1]-wvl[0]))
64        offsets[i] = spectrum_i.min()
65        if remove_offsets_individually:
66            spectrum.append(spectrum_i - offsets[i])
67            ax.plot(wvl, spectrum_i - offsets[i], label=f'Channel {i+1}')
68        else:
69            spectrum.append(spectrum_i)
70            ax.plot(wvl, spectrum_i, label=f'Channel {i+1}')
71
72    spectrum = np.mean(np.array(spectrum), axis=0)
73    ax.plot(wvl, spectrum, label='Mean spectrum')
74
75    return wvl, np.maximum(np.zeros(len(spectrum)), spectrum)

Reads a spectrum file from the Maya spectrometer and returns the wavelength and spectrum arrays.

The file is expected to have one column of wavelength data and arbitrarily many columns of equivalent spectra [to be averaged]. The function also applies a Gaussian filter to the spectrum data to smooth it. The function can optionally eliminate outliers in the spectrum data and remove offsets from each column individually.

Arguments:
  • filename
  • remove_offsets_individually (bool): If True, compute and remove offsets from each column individually
  • nm_smearing (float): sigma in nm of the gaussian filter applied to smooth the spectrum.
  • eliminate_outliers_spectrum (bool): = If True, eliminate single pixel outliers in the spectral data and replace them with average of surrounding values. default is False.
def read_spectrum_ocean_optics(filename): 
77def read_spectrum_ocean_optics(filename):
78    """Reads a spectrum file from the Ocean Optics spectrometer and returns the wavelength and spectrum arrays.
79    The file is expected to have one column of wavelength data and one column of spectrum data.
80    wavelengths are in nm.
81    14 lines of header are skipped."""
82    data = pandas.read_table(filename, sep='\t', keep_default_na=True, skiprows=14)

def asymmetric_tukey_f( x: float, edge1: float, edge2: float, edge1_width: float, edge2_width: float): 
 87def asymmetric_tukey_f(x: float, edge1: float, edge2: float, edge1_width: float, edge2_width: float):
 88
 89    if edge1_width < 0 or edge2_width < 0:
 90        edge1_width = 0
 91        edge2_width = 0
 92        print('Warning: negative tukey edge width; rectangular window computed')
 93    if abs(edge1_width) + abs(edge2_width) > 2 * abs(edge2 - edge1):
 94        raise Exception('Error: tukey edge width larger than admissible')
 95    if edge2 < edge1:
 96        e1 = edge2
 97        e2 = edge1
 98        w1 = edge2_width
 99        w2 = edge1_width
100    elif edge1 < edge2:
101        e1 = edge1
102        e2 = edge2
103        w1 = edge1_width
104        w2 = edge2_width
105    xmin = e1 - w1/2
106    xmax = e2 + w2/2
107    if x < xmin or x > xmax:
108        y = 0
109    elif xmin <= x and x < xmin + w1:
110        y = (1-np.cos((x-xmin)*np.pi/w1))/2
111    elif xmin + w1 <= x and x <= xmax - w2:
112        y = 1
113    elif xmax - w2 < x and x <= xmax:
114        y = (1-np.cos((x-xmax)*np.pi/w2))/2
115    else:
116        print ('x, xmax, xmin, w1, w2: ', x, xmax, xmin, w1, w2)
117        raise ValueError('in tukey_f, x could not be assigned correctly to the sub intervals, might it (or the other parameters) be NaN?')
118    return y
def asymmetric_tukey_window( x, edge1: float, edge2: float, edge1_width: float, edge2_width: float): 
120def asymmetric_tukey_window(x, edge1: float, edge2: float, edge1_width: float, edge2_width: float):
121
122    if isinstance(x, np.ndarray):
123        y = []
124        for xi in x:
125            y.append(asymmetric_tukey_f(xi, edge1, edge2, edge1_width, edge2_width))
126        y = np.array(y)
127    elif isinstance(x, list):
128        y = []
129        for xi in x:
130            y.append(asymmetric_tukey_f(xi, edge1, edge2, edge1_width, edge2_width))
131    elif isinstance(x, float):
132        y = asymmetric_tukey_f(x, edge1, edge2, edge1_width, edge2_width)
133    else:
134        raise TypeError('in function tukey window x is neither np array nor list nor float')
135    return y

137class SpectrumHandler:
138    """Class to perform standard operations on spectra (calibration, plotting, division, multiplication, etc.)"""
139
140    def __init__(self, filename: str = None, wavelengths = None, spectrum = None, remove_offsets_individually: bool=False, nm_smearing=1., eliminate_outliers_spectrum=False, filetype='MayaScarab'):
141        """Provide either a filename or the wavelengths and spectrum arrays to the constructor.
142
143        Args:
144            filename (str): Path to the file containing the spectrum data.
145            wavelengths and spectrum (np.ndarray): = Wavelengths and spectrum data arrays. (alternative to filename)
146            remove_offsets_individually (bool): = If True, compute and remove offsets from each column individually
147                (filename is expected to have one column of wavelength data and arbitrarily many columns of equivalent spectra [to be averaged]).
148            nm_smearing (float): Smearing in nm to be applied to the spectrum.
149            eliminate_outliers_spectrum (bool): If True, eliminate single pixel outliers in the spectral data and replace them with average of surrounding values.
150            filetype (str): Type of the file to be read. Options are 'MayaScarab' (default) or 'OceanOptics'.
151
152        """
153        self.nm_smearing = nm_smearing
154        self.wvl, self.spectrum = np.linspace(200, 1000, 800), np.zeros(800)
155        self.calibration_lamp_wvl, self.calibration_lamp_spectrum = None, None
156        self.calibration_factor = None
157
158        if filetype == 'MayaScarab' and filename is not None:
159            self.wvl, self.spectrum = read_spectrum_maya(filename, remove_offsets_individually, nm_smearing, eliminate_outliers_spectrum)
160        elif filetype == 'OceanOptics' and filename is not None:
161            self.wvl, self.spectrum = read_spectrum_ocean_optics(filename)
162        elif wavelengths is not None and spectrum is not None:
163            self.wvl = wavelengths
164            self.spectrum = spectrum
165        self.check_wvl_ascending()
166
167    def get_spectrum(self):
168        return self.wvl, self.spectrum
169
170    def get_calibration_factor(self):
171        if self.calibration_factor is None:
172            print("Warning: Calibration factor not available. Computing it from given spectra...")
173            self.compute_calibration_factor_spectrometer()
174        return self.wvl, self.calibration_factor
175
176    def calibrate(self):
177        """Applies the calibration factor to the spectrum and sets the calibration factor to None."""
178        if self.calibration_factor is None:
179            print("Warning: Calibration factor not available. Try load_calibration_factor_from_file(). Returning original spectrum.")
180        else:
181            self.spectrum = self.spectrum * self.calibration_factor
182            self.calibration_factor = None
183            print("Calibration factor applied to the spectrum. Calibration factor is now set to None.")
184
185    def save_to_file(self, filename):
186        if self.wvl is None or self.spectrum is None:
187            raise ValueError("Spectrum not loaded.")
188        data = pandas.DataFrame({'Wavelength': self.wvl, 'Spectrum': self.spectrum})
189        data.to_csv(filename, index=False, sep='\t')
190
191    def save_calibration_factor_to_file(self, filename):
192        """Saves the calibration factor to a file.
193
194        The file can be either a .txt, .csv or .npz file.
195        The file will contain the wavelength, calibration factor, calibration lamp true spectrum and measured lamp spectrum.
196        """
197
198        if self.calibration_factor is None:
199            raise ValueError("Calibration factor not computed.")
200        if '.txt' in filename or '.csv' in filename:
201            data = pandas.DataFrame({'Wavelength': self.wvl, 'Calibration Factor': self.calibration_factor,
202                                     'Lamp Spectrum': self.calibration_lamp_spectrum, 'Measured Spectrum': self.spectrum})
203            data.to_csv(filename, index=False, sep='\t')
204        elif '.npz' in filename:
205            np.savez(filename, wavelength=self.wvl, corr_factor_smoothed=self.calibration_factor,
206                     lamp_ref=self.calibration_lamp_spectrum, lamp_measured=self.spectrum)
207        else:
208            raise ValueError("File type not supported. Use .txt, .csv or .npz.")
209
210    def load_calibration_factor_from_file(self, filename):
211        data = pandas.read_table(filename, sep='\t', keep_default_na=True, skiprows=0)
212        self.calibration_factor = np.interp(self.wvl, np.array(data.iloc[:, 0]), np.array(data.iloc[:, 1]))
213
214    def check_wvl_ascending(self):
215        if self.wvl is not None and np.any(np.diff(self.wvl)) < 0:
216            if np.all(np.diff(self.wvl) < 0):
217                self.wvl = np.flip(self.wvl)
218                self.spectrum = np.flip(self.spectrum)
219            else:
220                raise ValueError("Wavelength array must be either in ascending or descending order.")
221        #same for calib spectrum
222        if self.calibration_lamp_wvl is not None and np.any(np.diff(self.calibration_lamp_wvl)) < 0:
223            if np.all(np.diff(self.calibration_lamp_wvl) < 0):
224                self.calibration_lamp_wvl = np.flip(self.calibration_lamp_wvl)
225                self.calibration_lamp_spectrum = np.flip(self.calibration_lamp_spectrum)
226            else:
227                raise ValueError("Wavelength array must be either in ascending or descending order.")
228        return True
229
230    def load_calibration_lamp_data(self, filename="./calibration_data/7315273LS-Deuterium-Halogen_CC-VISNIR.lmp"):
231        Data = pandas.read_table(filename)
232        self.calibration_lamp_wvl, self.calibration_lamp_spectrum = np.array(Data.iloc[:, 0]), np.array(Data.iloc[:, 1])
233        self.calibration_lamp_spectrum = gaussian_filter1d(self.calibration_lamp_spectrum,
234                                                self.nm_smearing / (self.calibration_lamp_wvl[1] - self.calibration_lamp_wvl[0]))
235        self.check_wvl_ascending()
236
237    def plot_calibration_data(self, low_lim=None, up_lim=None, low_lim_y=None, up_lim_y=None, wavelength_ROI: list = [420, 800]):
238        """Plot the calibration data of the lamp, the measured lamp spectrum, and the calibration factor.
239
240        The method assumes that the true calibration lamp data and the measured spectrum of the calibration lamp are loaded in the object
241        The normalization of the three curves is arbitrary. By default the region between 420 and 800 nm is used for normalization.
242
243        Args:
244            low_lim, up_lim(float): Wavelength limits for the x-axis.
245            low_lim_y, up_lim_y (float): Intensity limits for the y-axis.
246            wavelength_ROI (list): [wvl1, wvl2] = Wavelength range for the normalization of the calibration factor (for display purposes).
247                Default is [420, 800] nm.
248            """
249        if low_lim is None or up_lim is None:
250            low_lim = np.min(self.wvl)
251            up_lim = np.max(self.wvl)
252        if low_lim_y is None or up_lim_y is None:
253            low_lim_y = 0
254            up_lim_y = 3
255        fig, ax = plt.subplots()
256        ax.plot(self.wvl, self.spectrum / np.max(self.spectrum), label='spectrometer reading')
257        multipl_factor_lamp_plot = (self.spectrum[(self.wvl > wavelength_ROI[0])&(self.wvl < wavelength_ROI[1])].mean() /
258                                self.calibration_lamp_spectrum[(self.calibration_lamp_wvl > wavelength_ROI[0])&(self.calibration_lamp_wvl < wavelength_ROI[1])].mean())
259
260        ax.plot(self.calibration_lamp_wvl, self.calibration_lamp_spectrum / np.max(self.spectrum) * multipl_factor_lamp_plot,
261                label='actual lamp spectrum')
262        if self.calibration_factor is not None:
263            ax.plot(self.wvl, self.calibration_factor, label='calibration factor')
264        ax.set_xlabel('Wavelength (nm)')
265        ax.set_ylabel('Intensity (Arb. unit)')
266        ax.legend(loc='upper right')
267        ax.set_xlim(low_lim, up_lim)
268        ax.set_ylim(low_lim_y, up_lim_y)
269        return fig
270
271    def calibrate_wavelength_axis(self, intercept: float, slope: float):
272        """Calibrate the wavelength axis of the spectrum using the given coefficient of a linear fit.
273
274        Form of the calibration: true_wavelength = intercept + slope * measured_wavelength
275        The function modifies the wavelength axis in place.
276
277        Args:
278            intercept: float,
279            slope: float
280            """
281        if self.wvl is None or self.spectrum is None:
282            raise ValueError("Spectrum not loaded.")
283        self.wvl = intercept + slope * self.wvl
284        self.check_wvl_ascending()
285
286    def tukey_filter(self, edge1: float, edge2: float, edge1_width: float, edge2_width: float):
287        """Applies a Tukey window to the spectrum (e.g. to remove noise at the edges).
288
289        Tukey window is defined as:
290         * cosine-shaped window between edge1-edge1_width/2 and edge1+edge1_width/2
291         * 1 between edge1+edge1_width/2 and edge2-edge2_width/2
292         * cosine-shaped window between edge2-edge2_width/2 and edge2+edge2_width/2
293         * 0 everywhere else
294        In this case, tukey window is computed in the wavelength domain.
295
296        Args:
297            edge1, edge2 (float): Wavelength limits for the Tukey window (edge2-edge1 = FWHM, in nm)
298            edge1_width, edge2_width (float): Width of the cosine-shaped edge of the tukey window (in nm).
299            """
300
301        window = asymmetric_tukey_window(self.wvl, edge1, edge2, edge1_width, edge2_width)
302        self.spectrum = self.spectrum * window
303        if self.calibration_factor is not None:
304            self.calibration_factor = self.calibration_factor * window
305        if self.calibration_lamp_wvl is not None and self.calibration_lamp_spectrum is not None:
306            window = asymmetric_tukey_window(self.calibration_lamp_wvl, edge1, edge2, edge1_width, edge2_width)
307            self.calibration_lamp_spectrum = self.calibration_lamp_spectrum * window
308
309    def divide_by(self, spectrumObject, nm_smearing=0.):
310        """normalizes the current spectrum with another spectrum, and stores the result in the present object.
311
312        Args:
313            spectrumObject (either 'c'/'calib'/'calibration'/'lamp' or SpectrumHandler object):
314                the current spectrum is divided at each wavelength by the loaded calibration lamp data or by the spectrum passed as SpectrumHandler object.
315            nm_smearing (float): sigma in nm for the gaussian smoothing
316        """
317        if spectrumObject == 'c' or spectrumObject == 'calib' or spectrumObject == 'calibration' or spectrumObject == 'lamp' or spectrumObject == 'calibration data':
318            if self.calibration_lamp_wvl is None or self.calibration_lamp_spectrum is None:
319                raise ValueError("Calibration lamp data not loaded.")
320            wvl_divisor = self.calibration_lamp_wvl
321            spectrum_divisor = self.calibration_lamp_spectrum
322        elif not isinstance(spectrumObject, SpectrumHandler):
323            raise TypeError("Input of divide_by must be a SpectrumHandler object.")
324        else:
325            wvl_divisor, spectrum_divisor = spectrumObject.get_spectrum()
326
327        if nm_smearing > 0:
328            spectrum_divisor = gaussian_filter1d(spectrum_divisor, sigma=nm_smearing/(wvl_divisor[1]-wvl_divisor[0]))
329            self.spectrum = gaussian_filter1d(self.spectrum, sigma=nm_smearing/(self.wvl[1]-self.wvl[0]))
330        commonWvl = self.wvl[(self.wvl>np.min(wvl_divisor))&(self.wvl<np.max(wvl_divisor))]
331        interpolated_spd = np.interp(commonWvl, wvl_divisor, spectrum_divisor)
332        interpolated_original = np.interp(commonWvl, self.wvl, self.spectrum)
333        self.wvl = commonWvl
334        self.spectrum = interpolated_original / interpolated_spd
335
336    def add(self, spectrumObject):
337        """adds two spectra and stores the result in the present object
338
339        Args:
340            spectrumObject (SpectrumHandler): spectrum to be added
341        """
342        if not isinstance(spectrumObject, SpectrumHandler):
343            raise TypeError("Input of add must be a SpectrumHandler object.")
344        wvl_add, spectrum_add = spectrumObject.get_spectrum()
345        commonWvl = self.wvl[(self.wvl>np.min(wvl_add))&(self.wvl<np.max(wvl_add))]
346        interpolated_spd = np.interp(commonWvl, wvl_add, spectrum_add)
347        interpolated_original = np.interp(commonWvl, self.wvl, self.spectrum)
348        self.wvl = commonWvl
349        self.spectrum = interpolated_original + interpolated_spd
350
351    def multiply(self, spectrumObject):
352        """multiplies the current spectrum by a second one at each wavelength.
353
354        Args:
355            spectrumObject (SpectrumHandler)
356        """
357        if not isinstance(spectrumObject, SpectrumHandler):
358            raise TypeError("Input of multiply must be a SpectrumHandler object.")
359        wvl_mult, spectrum_mult = spectrumObject.get_spectrum()
360        commonWvl = self.wvl[(self.wvl>np.min(wvl_mult))&(self.wvl<np.max(wvl_mult))]
361        interpolated_spd = np.interp(commonWvl, wvl_mult, spectrum_mult)
362        interpolated_original = np.interp(commonWvl, self.wvl, self.spectrum)
363        self.wvl = commonWvl
364        self.spectrum = interpolated_original * interpolated_spd
365
366    def multiply_scalar(self, scalar):
367        """multiplies the current spectrum by a constant.
368
369        Args:
370            scalar (float)
371        """
372        self.spectrum = self.spectrum * scalar
373
374    def add_scalar(self, scalar):
375        """adds a constant offset.
376
377        Args:
378            scalar (float)
379        """
380        self.spectrum = self.spectrum + scalar
381
382    def compute_calibration_factor_spectrometer(self, transmission_additional_optics=None, smoothing='poly', extend_calibration: bool = False, wavelength_ROI: list = [420, 800]):
383        """Computes the calibration factor.
384
385         It assumes that in the SpectrumHandler object:
386         * the measured spectrum of the calibration lamp is loaded as main spectrum
387         * the true tabulated spectrum of the calibration lamp is loaded as self.calibration_lamp_spectrum [via load_calibration_lamp_data()]
388
389         Args:
390            transmission_additional_optics: list of SpectrumHandler objects = list of transmission spectra of additional optics to be taken into account when computing the calibration factor.
391                The transmission ['reflection' for mirrors] spectra of additional optics will be included (multiplied) in the calibration factor
392                Additional optics are assumed to be in the beam path of any standard measurement (e.g. integrating sphere) BUT NOT PRESENT during the calibration lamp measurement.
393            smoothing: Type of smoothing to be applied to the calibration factor. Options are 'poly' (default) None or an integer number. If 'poly', a polynomial fit is applied to the calibration factor.
394                If None, no smoothing is applied. If an integer number, a box filter of that size is applied to the calibration factor.
395            extend_calibration (bool): If True, the calibration factor is extended to the full wavelength range of the spectrometer (the first and last values of the calibration curve are used for the extension).
396                This is a quick and dirty solution to deal with the fact that the calibration lamp spectrum is not available for the full wavelength range of the spectrometer.
397            wavelength_ROI (list): [wvl1, wvl2] Wavelength range for the normalization of the calibration factor (for display purposes).
398                Default is [420, 800] nm."""
399        if self.calibration_lamp_wvl is None or self.calibration_lamp_spectrum is None:
400            raise ValueError("Calibration lamp data not loaded.")
401        wvl_stored, spectrum_stored = self.wvl, self.spectrum
402        self.divide_by('calibration data')
403
404        eliminate_outliers(self.spectrum, threshold=3, window_points=20)
405
406        if transmission_additional_optics is not None:
407            for sao in transmission_additional_optics:
408                if not isinstance(sao, SpectrumHandler):
409                    raise TypeError("Input of spectra_additional_optics must be a list of SpectrumHandler objects.")
410                wvl_sao, spectrum_sao = sao.get_spectrum()
411                if np.any(np.diff(wvl_sao)) < 0:
412                    raise ValueError("Wavelength array of additional optics spectrum must be sorted in ascending order.")
413                wvl_sao = np.concatenate((np.array([0]), wvl_sao, np.array([max(np.max(self.wvl), np.max(wvl_sao))])))
414                spectrum_sao = np.concatenate((np.array([spectrum_sao[0]]), spectrum_sao, np.array([spectrum_sao[-1]])))
415                self.spectrum = self.spectrum * np.interp(self.wvl, wvl_sao, spectrum_sao)
416
417        self.calibration_factor = self.spectrum
418        if smoothing is None:
419            pass
420        elif smoothing == 'poly':
421            smoothed_cf = np.poly1d(np.polyfit(self.wvl, self.calibration_factor, 50))
422            self.calibration_factor = smoothed_cf(self.wvl)
423        else:
424            if not isinstance(smoothing, int):
425                raise TypeError("Input of smoothing must be 'poly', None or an integer.")
426            if smoothing < 1:
427                raise ValueError("Input of smoothing must be a positive integer.")
428            self.calibration_factor = box_smooth(self.calibration_factor, smoothing)
429
430        for i in range(len(self.wvl)):
431            if self.calibration_factor[i] < 0.01:
432                self.calibration_factor[i] = 0.01
433        self.calibration_factor = 1/self.calibration_factor
434        self.calibration_factor = self.calibration_factor / np.mean(self.calibration_factor[
435            (self.wvl > wavelength_ROI[0]) & (self.wvl < wavelength_ROI[1])])
436
437        if extend_calibration:
438            # Extend the calibration factor to the full wavelength range of the spectrometer (pick the first and last values of the calibration curve for the extension)
439            self.wvl = np.concatenate((np.linspace(0, self.wvl[0], 100), self.wvl, np.linspace(self.wvl[-1], self.wvl[-1], 100)))
440            self.calibration_factor = np.concatenate((np.ones(100)*self.calibration_factor[0], self.calibration_factor, np.ones(100)*self.calibration_factor[-1]))
441            self.calibration_factor = np.interp(wvl_stored, self.wvl, self.calibration_factor)
442            self.wvl = wvl_stored
443            self.spectrum = spectrum_stored
444        else:
445            self.spectrum = spectrum_stored[(wvl_stored>np.min(self.calibration_lamp_wvl))&(wvl_stored<np.max(self.calibration_lamp_wvl))]
446
447    def plot_spectrum(self, low_lim=None, up_lim=None):
448        fig, ax = plt.subplots()
449        if low_lim is not None and up_lim is not None:
450            ax.plot(self.wvl[(self.wvl>low_lim)&(self.wvl<up_lim)], self.spectrum[(self.wvl>low_lim)&(self.wvl<up_lim)])
451        else:
452            ax.plot(self.wvl, self.spectrum)
453        ax.set_xlabel('Wavelength (nm)')
454        ax.set_ylabel('Intensity (Arb. unit)')
455        return fig

214    def check_wvl_ascending(self):
215        if self.wvl is not None and np.any(np.diff(self.wvl)) < 0:
216            if np.all(np.diff(self.wvl) < 0):
217                self.wvl = np.flip(self.wvl)
218                self.spectrum = np.flip(self.spectrum)
219            else:
220                raise ValueError("Wavelength array must be either in ascending or descending order.")
221        #same for calib spectrum
222        if self.calibration_lamp_wvl is not None and np.any(np.diff(self.calibration_lamp_wvl)) < 0:
223            if np.all(np.diff(self.calibration_lamp_wvl) < 0):
224                self.calibration_lamp_wvl = np.flip(self.calibration_lamp_wvl)
225                self.calibration_lamp_spectrum = np.flip(self.calibration_lamp_spectrum)
226            else:
227                raise ValueError("Wavelength array must be either in ascending or descending order.")
228        return True

def plot_calibration_data( self, low_lim=None, up_lim=None, low_lim_y=None, up_lim_y=None, wavelength_ROI: list = [420, 800]): 
237    def plot_calibration_data(self, low_lim=None, up_lim=None, low_lim_y=None, up_lim_y=None, wavelength_ROI: list = [420, 800]):
238        """Plot the calibration data of the lamp, the measured lamp spectrum, and the calibration factor.
239
240        The method assumes that the true calibration lamp data and the measured spectrum of the calibration lamp are loaded in the object
241        The normalization of the three curves is arbitrary. By default the region between 420 and 800 nm is used for normalization.
242
243        Args:
244            low_lim, up_lim(float): Wavelength limits for the x-axis.
245            low_lim_y, up_lim_y (float): Intensity limits for the y-axis.
246            wavelength_ROI (list): [wvl1, wvl2] = Wavelength range for the normalization of the calibration factor (for display purposes).
247                Default is [420, 800] nm.
248            """
249        if low_lim is None or up_lim is None:
250            low_lim = np.min(self.wvl)
251            up_lim = np.max(self.wvl)
252        if low_lim_y is None or up_lim_y is None:
253            low_lim_y = 0
254            up_lim_y = 3
255        fig, ax = plt.subplots()
256        ax.plot(self.wvl, self.spectrum / np.max(self.spectrum), label='spectrometer reading')
257        multipl_factor_lamp_plot = (self.spectrum[(self.wvl > wavelength_ROI[0])&(self.wvl < wavelength_ROI[1])].mean() /
258                                self.calibration_lamp_spectrum[(self.calibration_lamp_wvl > wavelength_ROI[0])&(self.calibration_lamp_wvl < wavelength_ROI[1])].mean())
259
260        ax.plot(self.calibration_lamp_wvl, self.calibration_lamp_spectrum / np.max(self.spectrum) * multipl_factor_lamp_plot,
261                label='actual lamp spectrum')
262        if self.calibration_factor is not None:
263            ax.plot(self.wvl, self.calibration_factor, label='calibration factor')
264        ax.set_xlabel('Wavelength (nm)')
265        ax.set_ylabel('Intensity (Arb. unit)')
266        ax.legend(loc='upper right')
267        ax.set_xlim(low_lim, up_lim)
268        ax.set_ylim(low_lim_y, up_lim_y)
269        return fig

def calibrate_wavelength_axis(self, intercept: float, slope: float): 
271    def calibrate_wavelength_axis(self, intercept: float, slope: float):
272        """Calibrate the wavelength axis of the spectrum using the given coefficient of a linear fit.
273
274        Form of the calibration: true_wavelength = intercept + slope * measured_wavelength
275        The function modifies the wavelength axis in place.
276
277        Args:
278            intercept: float,
279            slope: float
280            """
281        if self.wvl is None or self.spectrum is None:
282            raise ValueError("Spectrum not loaded.")
283        self.wvl = intercept + slope * self.wvl
284        self.check_wvl_ascending()

def tukey_filter( self, edge1: float, edge2: float, edge1_width: float, edge2_width: float): 
286    def tukey_filter(self, edge1: float, edge2: float, edge1_width: float, edge2_width: float):
287        """Applies a Tukey window to the spectrum (e.g. to remove noise at the edges).
288
289        Tukey window is defined as:
290         * cosine-shaped window between edge1-edge1_width/2 and edge1+edge1_width/2
291         * 1 between edge1+edge1_width/2 and edge2-edge2_width/2
292         * cosine-shaped window between edge2-edge2_width/2 and edge2+edge2_width/2
293         * 0 everywhere else
294        In this case, tukey window is computed in the wavelength domain.
295
296        Args:
297            edge1, edge2 (float): Wavelength limits for the Tukey window (edge2-edge1 = FWHM, in nm)
298            edge1_width, edge2_width (float): Width of the cosine-shaped edge of the tukey window (in nm).
299            """
300
301        window = asymmetric_tukey_window(self.wvl, edge1, edge2, edge1_width, edge2_width)
302        self.spectrum = self.spectrum * window
303        if self.calibration_factor is not None:
304            self.calibration_factor = self.calibration_factor * window
305        if self.calibration_lamp_wvl is not None and self.calibration_lamp_spectrum is not None:
306            window = asymmetric_tukey_window(self.calibration_lamp_wvl, edge1, edge2, edge1_width, edge2_width)
307            self.calibration_lamp_spectrum = self.calibration_lamp_spectrum * window

Applies a Tukey window to the spectrum (e.g. to remove noise at the edges).

Tukey window is defined as:
  • cosine-shaped window between edge1-edge1_width/2 and edge1+edge1_width/2
  • 1 between edge1+edge1_width/2 and edge2-edge2_width/2
  • cosine-shaped window between edge2-edge2_width/2 and edge2+edge2_width/2
  • 0 everywhere else

In this case, tukey window is computed in the wavelength domain.

Arguments:
  • edge1, edge2 (float): Wavelength limits for the Tukey window (edge2-edge1 = FWHM, in nm)
  • edge1_width, edge2_width (float): Width of the cosine-shaped edge of the tukey window (in nm).
def divide_by(self, spectrumObject, nm_smearing=0.0): 
309    def divide_by(self, spectrumObject, nm_smearing=0.):
310        """normalizes the current spectrum with another spectrum, and stores the result in the present object.
311
312        Args:
313            spectrumObject (either 'c'/'calib'/'calibration'/'lamp' or SpectrumHandler object):
314                the current spectrum is divided at each wavelength by the loaded calibration lamp data or by the spectrum passed as SpectrumHandler object.
315            nm_smearing (float): sigma in nm for the gaussian smoothing
316        """
317        if spectrumObject == 'c' or spectrumObject == 'calib' or spectrumObject == 'calibration' or spectrumObject == 'lamp' or spectrumObject == 'calibration data':
318            if self.calibration_lamp_wvl is None or self.calibration_lamp_spectrum is None:
319                raise ValueError("Calibration lamp data not loaded.")
320            wvl_divisor = self.calibration_lamp_wvl
321            spectrum_divisor = self.calibration_lamp_spectrum
322        elif not isinstance(spectrumObject, SpectrumHandler):
323            raise TypeError("Input of divide_by must be a SpectrumHandler object.")
324        else:
325            wvl_divisor, spectrum_divisor = spectrumObject.get_spectrum()
326
327        if nm_smearing > 0:
328            spectrum_divisor = gaussian_filter1d(spectrum_divisor, sigma=nm_smearing/(wvl_divisor[1]-wvl_divisor[0]))
329            self.spectrum = gaussian_filter1d(self.spectrum, sigma=nm_smearing/(self.wvl[1]-self.wvl[0]))
330        commonWvl = self.wvl[(self.wvl>np.min(wvl_divisor))&(self.wvl<np.max(wvl_divisor))]
331        interpolated_spd = np.interp(commonWvl, wvl_divisor, spectrum_divisor)
332        interpolated_original = np.interp(commonWvl, self.wvl, self.spectrum)
333        self.wvl = commonWvl
334        self.spectrum = interpolated_original / interpolated_spd

normalizes the current spectrum with another spectrum, and stores the result in the present object.

Arguments:
  • spectrumObject (either 'c'/'calib'/'calibration'/'lamp' or SpectrumHandler object): the current spectrum is divided at each wavelength by the loaded calibration lamp data or by the spectrum passed as SpectrumHandler object.
  • nm_smearing (float): sigma in nm for the gaussian smoothing

def compute_calibration_factor_spectrometer( self, transmission_additional_optics=None, smoothing='poly', extend_calibration: bool = False, wavelength_ROI: list = [420, 800]): 
382    def compute_calibration_factor_spectrometer(self, transmission_additional_optics=None, smoothing='poly', extend_calibration: bool = False, wavelength_ROI: list = [420, 800]):
383        """Computes the calibration factor.
384
385         It assumes that in the SpectrumHandler object:
386         * the measured spectrum of the calibration lamp is loaded as main spectrum
387         * the true tabulated spectrum of the calibration lamp is loaded as self.calibration_lamp_spectrum [via load_calibration_lamp_data()]
388
389         Args:
390            transmission_additional_optics: list of SpectrumHandler objects = list of transmission spectra of additional optics to be taken into account when computing the calibration factor.
391                The transmission ['reflection' for mirrors] spectra of additional optics will be included (multiplied) in the calibration factor
392                Additional optics are assumed to be in the beam path of any standard measurement (e.g. integrating sphere) BUT NOT PRESENT during the calibration lamp measurement.
393            smoothing: Type of smoothing to be applied to the calibration factor. Options are 'poly' (default) None or an integer number. If 'poly', a polynomial fit is applied to the calibration factor.
394                If None, no smoothing is applied. If an integer number, a box filter of that size is applied to the calibration factor.
395            extend_calibration (bool): If True, the calibration factor is extended to the full wavelength range of the spectrometer (the first and last values of the calibration curve are used for the extension).
396                This is a quick and dirty solution to deal with the fact that the calibration lamp spectrum is not available for the full wavelength range of the spectrometer.
397            wavelength_ROI (list): [wvl1, wvl2] Wavelength range for the normalization of the calibration factor (for display purposes).
398                Default is [420, 800] nm."""
399        if self.calibration_lamp_wvl is None or self.calibration_lamp_spectrum is None:
400            raise ValueError("Calibration lamp data not loaded.")
401        wvl_stored, spectrum_stored = self.wvl, self.spectrum
402        self.divide_by('calibration data')
403
404        eliminate_outliers(self.spectrum, threshold=3, window_points=20)
405
406        if transmission_additional_optics is not None:
407            for sao in transmission_additional_optics:
408                if not isinstance(sao, SpectrumHandler):
409                    raise TypeError("Input of spectra_additional_optics must be a list of SpectrumHandler objects.")
410                wvl_sao, spectrum_sao = sao.get_spectrum()
411                if np.any(np.diff(wvl_sao)) < 0:
412                    raise ValueError("Wavelength array of additional optics spectrum must be sorted in ascending order.")
413                wvl_sao = np.concatenate((np.array([0]), wvl_sao, np.array([max(np.max(self.wvl), np.max(wvl_sao))])))
414                spectrum_sao = np.concatenate((np.array([spectrum_sao[0]]), spectrum_sao, np.array([spectrum_sao[-1]])))
415                self.spectrum = self.spectrum * np.interp(self.wvl, wvl_sao, spectrum_sao)
416
417        self.calibration_factor = self.spectrum
418        if smoothing is None:
419            pass
420        elif smoothing == 'poly':
421            smoothed_cf = np.poly1d(np.polyfit(self.wvl, self.calibration_factor, 50))
422            self.calibration_factor = smoothed_cf(self.wvl)
423        else:
424            if not isinstance(smoothing, int):
425                raise TypeError("Input of smoothing must be 'poly', None or an integer.")
426            if smoothing < 1:
427                raise ValueError("Input of smoothing must be a positive integer.")
428            self.calibration_factor = box_smooth(self.calibration_factor, smoothing)
429
430        for i in range(len(self.wvl)):
431            if self.calibration_factor[i] < 0.01:
432                self.calibration_factor[i] = 0.01
433        self.calibration_factor = 1/self.calibration_factor
434        self.calibration_factor = self.calibration_factor / np.mean(self.calibration_factor[
435            (self.wvl > wavelength_ROI[0]) & (self.wvl < wavelength_ROI[1])])
436
437        if extend_calibration:
438            # Extend the calibration factor to the full wavelength range of the spectrometer (pick the first and last values of the calibration curve for the extension)
439            self.wvl = np.concatenate((np.linspace(0, self.wvl[0], 100), self.wvl, np.linspace(self.wvl[-1], self.wvl[-1], 100)))
440            self.calibration_factor = np.concatenate((np.ones(100)*self.calibration_factor[0], self.calibration_factor, np.ones(100)*self.calibration_factor[-1]))
441            self.calibration_factor = np.interp(wvl_stored, self.wvl, self.calibration_factor)
442            self.wvl = wvl_stored
443            self.spectrum = spectrum_stored
444        else:
445            self.spectrum = spectrum_stored[(wvl_stored>np.min(self.calibration_lamp_wvl))&(wvl_stored<np.max(self.calibration_lamp_wvl))]

Computes the calibration factor.

It assumes that in the SpectrumHandler object:

  • the measured spectrum of the calibration lamp is loaded as main spectrum
  • the true tabulated spectrum of the calibration lamp is loaded as self.calibration_lamp_spectrum [via load_calibration_lamp_data()]
Arguments:
  • transmission_additional_optics: list of SpectrumHandler objects = list of transmission spectra of additional optics to be taken into account when computing the calibration factor. The transmission ['reflection' for mirrors] spectra of additional optics will be included (multiplied) in the calibration factor Additional optics are assumed to be in the beam path of any standard measurement (e.g. integrating sphere) BUT NOT PRESENT during the calibration lamp measurement.
  • smoothing: Type of smoothing to be applied to the calibration factor. Options are 'poly' (default) None or an integer number. If 'poly', a polynomial fit is applied to the calibration factor. If None, no smoothing is applied. If an integer number, a box filter of that size is applied to the calibration factor.
  • extend_calibration (bool): If True, the calibration factor is extended to the full wavelength range of the spectrometer (the first and last values of the calibration curve are used for the extension). This is a quick and dirty solution to deal with the fact that the calibration lamp spectrum is not available for the full wavelength range of the spectrometer.
  • wavelength_ROI (list): [wvl1, wvl2] Wavelength range for the normalization of the calibration factor (for display purposes). Default is [420, 800] nm.

class MultiSpectrumHandler: 
459class MultiSpectrumHandler:
460    """Stores and plots multiple spectra"""
461    def __init__(self, filenameList: list = None, wavelengthList: list = None, spectrumList: list = None, spectrumHandlerList: list = None, remove_offsets_individually: bool=False, nm_smearing=1., eliminate_outliers_spectrum=False, filetype='MayaScarab'):
462        """Constructor for the MultiSpectrumHandler class.
463
464        Args:
465            filenameList: list = List of filenames to be read.
466            wavelengthList: list = List of wavelength arrays. (alternative to filename)
467            spectrumList: list = List of spectrum arrays. (alternative to filename)
468            remove_offsets_individually: bool = If True, compute and remove offsets from each column individually
469                (filename is expected to have one column of wavelength data and arbitrarily many columns of equivalent spectra [to be averaged]).
470            nm_smearing: float = Smearing in nm to be applied to the spectrum.
471            eliminate_outliers_spectrum: bool = If True, eliminate single pixel outliers in the spectral data and replace them with average of surrounding values.
472            filetype: str = Type of the file to be read. Options are 'MayaScarab' (default) or 'OceanOptics'."""
473        self.spectrumHandlers = []
474        if filenameList is not None:
475            for filename in filenameList:
476                self.spectrumHandlers.append(SpectrumHandler(filename=filename, remove_offsets_individually=remove_offsets_individually,
477                                                             nm_smearing=nm_smearing, eliminate_outliers_spectrum=eliminate_outliers_spectrum, filetype=filetype))
478        elif wavelengthList is not None and spectrumList is not None:
479            for i in range(len(wavelengthList)):
480                self.spectrumHandlers.append(SpectrumHandler(wavelengths=wavelengthList[i], spectrum=spectrumList[i],
481                                                             remove_offsets_individually=remove_offsets_individually, nm_smearing=nm_smearing,
482                                                             eliminate_outliers_spectrum=eliminate_outliers_spectrum, filetype=filetype))
483        elif spectrumHandlerList is not None:
484            for spectrumHandler in spectrumHandlerList:
485                if not isinstance(spectrumHandler, SpectrumHandler):
486                    raise TypeError("Input of spectrumHandlerList must be a list of SpectrumHandler objects.")
487                self.spectrumHandlers.append(spectrumHandler)
488        else:
489            raise ValueError("Either filenameList or wavelengthList and spectrumList or spectrumHandlerList must be provided. filetype, if provided, can only be 'MayaScarab' or 'OceanOptics'.")
490
491    def plot(self, low_lim = None, up_lim = None):
492        fig, ax = plt.subplots()
493        for i, spectrumHandler in enumerate(self.spectrumHandlers):
494            wvl, spectrum = spectrumHandler.get_spectrum()
495            if low_lim is not None and up_lim is not None:
496                ax.plot(wvl[(wvl>low_lim)&(wvl<up_lim)], spectrum[(wvl>low_lim)&(wvl<up_lim)], label=f'Spectrum {i+1}')
497            else:
498                ax.plot(wvl, spectrum, label=f'Spectrum {i+1}')
499        ax.set_xlabel('Wavelength (nm)')
500        ax.set_ylabel('Intensity (Arb. unit)')
501        ax.legend(loc='upper right')
502        return fig
